sentences.zh: 劉三吾，茶陵人。

translations.literal: Liu Sanwu was a native of Chaling.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sanwu came from Chaling.

sentences.zh: 初名如孫，以字行。

translations.literal: His original name was Rusun; he was known by his style name.
translations.idiomatic: Born Rusun, he went by his style name Sanwu.

sentences.zh: 兄耕孫、燾孫皆仕元。

translations.literal: His elder brothers Gengsun and Taosun both served the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brothers Gengsun and Taosun had both held office under the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 耕孫，寧國路推官，死長槍賊難。

translations.literal: Gengsun was pushan of Ningguo Route and died in the turmoil of the Changqiang bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Gengsun had been investigating censor of Ningguo Route and perished in the uprising of the Long-Spear bandits.

sentences.zh: 燾孫，常寧州學正，死僚寇。

translations.literal: Taosun was director of studies at Changning Prefecture and died at the hands of Liao raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Taosun had been director of studies at Changning Prefecture and was killed by Liao marauders.

sentences.zh: 三吾避兵廣西，行省承制授靜江路儒學副提舉。

translations.literal: Sanwu fled the warfare to Guangxi, where the provincial administration appointed him by provisional commission as vice promoter of learning at Jingjiang Route.
translations.idiomatic: Sanwu took refuge from the fighting in Guangxi, where the provincial government provisionally appointed him vice promoter of learning on the Jingjiang circuit.

sentences.zh: 明兵下廣西，乃歸茶陵。

translations.literal: When Ming forces took Guangxi, he returned to Chaling.
translations.idiomatic: After Ming troops pacified Guangxi, he went home to Chaling.

sentences.zh: 洪武十八年，以茹常薦召至，年七十三矣，奏對稱旨，授左贊善，累遷翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Hongwu, on Ru Chang's recommendation he was summoned to court; he was already seventy-three. His answers in audience pleased the throne, and he was appointed Left Tutor in Virtue, then promoted repeatedly to Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 18, on Ru Chang's recommendation he was called to court at the age of seventy-three. His replies in audience pleased the Emperor, who made him Left Tutor in Virtue and soon promoted him to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 時天下初平，典章闕略。

translations.literal: The realm had only just been pacified, and the ritual code was still incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: The empire had only lately been pacified, and its institutions and ritual code were still rudimentary.

sentences.zh: 帝銳意制作，宿儒雕謝，得三吾晚，悅之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was keen to establish institutions and compose canonical works; veteran scholars had withered away one after another. He gained Sanwu only late, and was delighted with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was intent on establishing institutions and composing canonical works, but veteran scholars had died off one after another. He gained Sanwu only late in life and was greatly pleased with him.

sentences.zh: 一切禮制及三場取士法多所刊定。

translations.literal: He revised and settled much of the ritual system and the method of selecting scholars in the three examination sessions.
translations.idiomatic: Sanwu revised and settled much of the ritual code and the regulations for selecting scholars in the three examination sessions.

sentences.zh: 三吾博學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Sanwu was broadly learned and skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Sanwu was broadly learned and a skilled writer.

sentences.zh: 帝制《大誥》及《洪範註》成，皆命為序。

translations.literal: When the Emperor finished the 《Grand Admonitions》 and the 《Commentary on the Hongfan》, he ordered Sanwu to compose prefaces for both.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor completed the 《Grand Admonitions》 and the 《Commentary on the Hongfan》, he ordered Sanwu to write prefaces for both.

sentences.zh: 敕修《省躬錄》、《書傳會選》、《寰宇通志》、《禮制集要》諸書，皆總其事，賜賚甚厚。

translations.literal: When ordered to compile the 《Record of Self-Examination》, 《Selected Assembly of the Book of Documents》, 《Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm》, and 《Collected Essentials of Ritual Institutions》, among other works, Sanwu directed them all and received very generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to compile works such as the 《Record of Self-Examination》, 《Selected Assembly of the Book of Documents》, 《Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm》, and 《Collected Essentials of Ritual Institutions》, he directed them all and received lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗曰：「朕觀奎壁間嘗有黑氣，今消矣，文運其興乎。

translations.literal: The Emperor once said: "I have observed that there was once a dark vapor between Quibi; it has now vanished. Will the literary fortune rise again?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once said, "I have seen a dark vapor between the Qu and Bi constellations; it has now cleared. Is the literary fortune about to rise again?

sentences.zh: 卿等宜有所述作，以稱朕意。」

translations.literal: You gentlemen ought to produce writings to match my intent."
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen ought to produce writings that answer my wish."

sentences.zh: 帝制詩，時令屬和。

translations.literal: When the Emperor composed verse, Sanwu was often ordered to harmonize on seasonal themes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor composed poetry, Sanwu was often ordered to supply matching verses on the seasons.

sentences.zh: 嘗賜以朝鮮玳瑁筆。

translations.literal: He was once presented with a Korean tortoiseshell pen.
translations.idiomatic: He was once given a tortoiseshell pen from Korea.

sentences.zh: 朝參，命列侍衛前；

translations.literal: At court audience he was ordered to stand in the line before the guards;
translations.idiomatic: At court audience he was ordered to stand before the guards;

sentences.zh: 燕享，賜坐殿中。

translations.literal: at banquet feasts he was granted a seat in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: at banquets he was granted a seat in the hall.

sentences.zh: 與汪睿、朱善稱「三老。」

translations.literal: With Wang Rui and Zhu Shan he was called the "Three Elders."
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Rui and Zhu Shan he was styled the "Three Elders."

sentences.zh: 既而三吾年日益老，才力日益減，往往忤意，禮遇亦漸輕。

translations.literal: As Sanwu grew ever older his talent gradually waned; he often offended the Emperor's wishes, and the marks of honor shown him grew lighter.
translations.idiomatic: As Sanwu grew older his powers waned; he often displeased the Emperor, and the honors shown him gradually diminished.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，授晉世子經，吏部侍郎侯庸劾其怠職。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was assigned to instruct the heir of Jin; Vice Minister of Personnel Hou Yong impeached him for neglect of duty.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was assigned to instruct the heir of the Prince of Jin; Vice Minister of Personnel Hou Yong impeached him for neglect of duty.

sentences.zh: 降國子博士，尋還職。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Erudite of the National University, then soon restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to erudite of the National University, but was soon restored to his post.

sentences.zh: 琮起刑部檢校。

translations.literal: Cong began as a reviewing clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cong rose from a reviewing clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 鄉人楊士奇輩貴顯，琮無所攀援。

translations.literal: Fellow townsman Yang Shiji and his cohort had risen to high eminence, but Cong had no patron to whom he could attach himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow townsman Yang Shiji and his circle had risen to high eminence, yet Cong had no patron on whom he could rely.

sentences.zh: 宣德中猶以檢討掌助教事，卒官。

translations.literal: In the Xuande reign he still served as compiling editor managing assistant tutor duties, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuande reign he still served as a compiling editor in charge of assistant tutor duties, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 汪睿，字仲魯，婺源人。

translations.literal: Wang Rui, style name Zhonglu, was a native of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rui, styled Zhonglu, came from Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 元末與弟同集眾保鄉邑，助復饒州。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan he and his younger brother Tong gathered men to defend their home district and helped recover Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan he and his younger brother Tong raised a force to defend their home district and helped recover Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 授浮梁州同知，不就。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice prefect of Fuliang Prefecture but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered the post of vice prefect of Fuliang but declined it.

sentences.zh: 胡大海克休寧，睿兄弟來附，設星源翼分院於婺源，以同為院判。

translations.literal: When Hu Dahai took Xiuning, the Wang brothers came over to him; they established the Xingyuan wing sub-circuit at Wuyuan and made Tong its vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Dahai captured Xiuning, the Wang brothers submitted to him, established the Xingyuan wing sub-circuit at Wuyuan, and made Tong its vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 睿歸田裏。

translations.literal: Rui returned to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: Rui retired to his home village.

sentences.zh: 庚子秋，同將兵爭鄱陽，不克，棄妻孥，亡之浙西。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the gengzi year Tong led troops to contest Poyang but failed; he abandoned wife and children and fled to western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the gengzi year Tong led troops to contest Poyang but was defeated; he abandoned his wife and children and fled to western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 幕府疑之，檄睿入應天為質。

translations.literal: The headquarters grew suspicious and ordered Rui to come to Yingtian as a hostage.
translations.idiomatic: The headquarters grew suspicious and summoned Rui to Yingtian as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 已，聞同為張士誠所殺，乃授睿安慶稅令。

translations.literal: Later, hearing that Tong had been killed by Zhang Shicheng, they appointed Rui tax commissioner of Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: Later, learning that Tong had been killed by Zhang Shicheng, the court appointed Rui tax commissioner of Anqing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，征參贊川蜀軍事。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned to assist in military affairs in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned to assist in the Sichuan campaign.

sentences.zh: 以疾辭去。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 洪武十七年，復召見，命講《西伯戡黎》篇，授左春坊左司直。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Hongwu he was summoned again, ordered to lecture on the 《King Wu's Campaign against Li》 chapter, and appointed Left Rectifier of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 17 he was summoned again, ordered to lecture on the 《King Wu's Campaign against Li》 chapter, and appointed Left Rectifier of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 常命續《薰風自南來》詩及他應制，皆稱旨。

translations.literal: He was often ordered to continue the poem 《The Fragrant Wind Comes from the South》 and other compositions on imperial command; all pleased the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He was often ordered to continue the poem 《The Fragrant Wind Comes from the South》 and other compositions on imperial command, and all met with approval.

sentences.zh: 請春夏停決死罪，體天地生物之仁，從之。

translations.literal: He requested that capital sentences be suspended in spring and summer, in keeping with Heaven and Earth's benevolence in giving life; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that executions be suspended in spring and summer in accord with Heaven and Earth's benevolence in nurturing life, and the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 逾年，疾作，請假歸。

translations.literal: After a year illness set in and he asked leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he fell ill and asked leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 睿敦實閑靜，不妄言笑，及進講，遇事輒言。

translations.literal: Rui was solid, quiet, and ungiven to idle talk or laughter, yet when he lectured at court he spoke out whenever the occasion arose.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was solid and reserved, seldom laughing or speaking idly, yet when he lectured at court he spoke frankly whenever the occasion arose.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗以「善人」呼之。

translations.literal: The Emperor once called him a "good man."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once called him a "good man."

sentences.zh: 朱善，字備萬，豐城人。

translations.literal: Zhu Shan, style name Beiwang, was a native of Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shan, styled Beiwang, came from Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 九歲通經史大義，能屬文。

translations.literal: At nine he mastered the broad meaning of the classics and histories and could compose prose.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he had mastered the broad meaning of the classics and histories and could write prose.

sentences.zh: 元末兵亂，隱山中，事繼母以孝聞。

translations.literal: When warfare engulfed the realm at the end of the Yuan, he hid in the mountains and was known for his filial service to his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: When warfare engulfed the realm at the end of the Yuan, he lived in seclusion in the mountains and was known for his filial care of his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，為南昌教授。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu he served as professor at Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongwu reign he served as professor at Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 八年，廷對第一，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he placed first in the palace examination and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he placed first in the palace examination and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 逾年，奏對失旨，改典籍，放還鄉。

translations.literal: After a year his answers in audience missed the Emperor's intent; he was transferred to archivist and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: A year later his answers in audience displeased the Emperor; he was transferred to archivist and sent home.

sentences.zh: 復召為翰林待詔。

translations.literal: He was summoned again as Hanlin awaiting edict.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned again as a Hanlin awaiting edict.

sentences.zh: 上疏論婚姻律曰：「民間姑舅及兩姨子女，法不得為婚。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial on the marriage law, saying: "Among the people, children of paternal uncles and aunts and of maternal aunts on both sides are forbidden by law to marry.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial on the marriage law, saying, "Among the people, marriage between children of paternal uncles and aunts and of maternal aunts on both sides is forbidden by law.

sentences.zh: 仇家詆訟，或已聘見絕，或既婚復離，甚至兒女成行，有司逼奪。

translations.literal: Enemy families bring slander suits; some betrothals are broken off, some marriages already contracted are dissolved, and in extreme cases where sons and daughters have already grown up, officials force the families apart.
translations.idiomatic: Rival families bring suits; betrothals are broken off, marriages already contracted are dissolved, and in extreme cases where children have already grown up, officials force the families apart.

sentences.zh: 按舊律：尊長卑幼相與為婚者有禁。

translations.literal: According to the old statute, marriage between persons of senior and junior standing is forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: According to the old statute, marriage between persons of unequal generational standing is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 蓋謂母之姊妹，與己之身，是為姑舅兩姨，不可以卑幼上匹尊屬。

translations.literal: This means that one's mother's sisters, being of one's own generation, are termed paternal-aunt and maternal-aunt relations; a junior may not marry upward to a senior relation.
translations.idiomatic: This refers to one's mother's sisters, who stand in the relation of paternal aunt and maternal aunt to oneself; a junior may not marry a senior kinswoman.

sentences.zh: 若姑舅兩姨子女，無尊卑之嫌。

translations.literal: But among children of paternal uncles and aunts and of maternal aunts on both sides there is no question of senior and junior.
translations.idiomatic: But among children of paternal uncles and aunts and of maternal aunts on both sides there is no question of senior and junior standing.

sentences.zh: 成周時，王朝相與為婚者，不過齊、宋、陳、杞。

translations.literal: In the age of the Cheng Zhou, the royal house intermarried with no more than Qi, Song, Chen, and Qi of the cadet line.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of the Cheng Zhou, the royal house intermarried with no more than Qi, Song, Chen, and Qi of the cadet line.

sentences.zh: 故稱異姓大國曰「伯舅」，小國曰「叔舅」。

translations.literal: Hence great states of different surnames were called "elder uncle by marriage," and small states "younger uncle by marriage."
translations.idiomatic: Hence great states of different surnames were called "elder uncle by marriage," and small states "younger uncle by marriage."

sentences.zh: 列國齊、宋、魯、秦、晉，亦各自為甥舅之國。

translations.literal: Among the feudal states Qi, Song, Lu, Qin, and Jin likewise each formed networks of marriage between nephews and uncles.
translations.idiomatic: Among the feudal states Qi, Song, Lu, Qin, and Jin likewise each formed networks of marriage between nephews and uncles.

sentences.zh: 後世，晉王、謝，唐崔、盧，潘、楊之睦，朱、陳之好，皆世為婚媾。

translations.literal: In later ages the Wang and Xie clans of Jin, the Cui and Lu clans of Tang, the friendly houses of Pan and Yang, and the close ties of Zhu and Chen—all maintained marriage alliances for generations.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages the Wang and Xie of Jin, the Cui and Lu of Tang, the friendly houses of Pan and Yang, and the close ties of Zhu and Chen—all maintained marriage alliances for generations.

sentences.zh: 溫嶠以舅子娶姑女，呂滎公夫人張氏即其母申國夫人姊女。

translations.literal: Wen Jiao, as his mother's sister's son, married his father's sister's daughter; Lady Zhang, wife of the Duke of Lü from Ying, was her mother's elder sister's daughter from the Lady of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiao married his paternal aunt's daughter though he was his maternal aunt's son; Lady Zhang, wife of the Duke of Lü from Ying, was her mother's elder sister's daughter.

sentences.zh: 古人如此甚多，願下群臣議，馳其禁。」

translations.literal: The ancients did likewise in very many cases. I beg that Your Majesty submit the matter to the ministers for deliberation and lift this prohibition."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients did likewise in very many cases. I beg that Your Majesty submit the matter to the ministers for deliberation and lift this prohibition."

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor granted the request.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor granted the request.

sentences.zh: 十八年擢文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Grand Academician of the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Grand Academician of the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 嘗講《家人卦》、《心箴》，帝大悅。

translations.literal: He once lectured on the 《Family》 hexagram and the 《Heart Admonition》; the Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He once lectured on the 《Family》 hexagram and the 《Heart Admonition》, and the Emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 未幾，請告歸。

translations.literal: Before long he asked leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he asked leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十二。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 著有《詩經解頤》、《史輯》傳於世。

translations.literal: He authored the 《Exegesis of the Odes for Nourishing the Cheeks》 and 《Historical Compendium》, which were handed down in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works 《Exegesis of the Odes for Nourishing the Cheeks》 and 《Historical Compendium》 have been handed down.

sentences.zh: 正德中，謚文恪。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign he was given the posthumous title Wenge.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengde reign he was given the posthumous title Wenge.

sentences.zh: 安然，祥符人，徙居潁州。

translations.literal: An Ran was a native of Xiangfu and later moved to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An Ran came from Xiangfu and later moved to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 元季以左丞守萊州。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan he served as left councillor defending Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan he served as left councillor defending Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 明兵下山東，率眾歸附。

translations.literal: When Ming forces descended on Shandong, he led his followers to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming forces entered Shandong, he led his followers in submission.

sentences.zh: 累官山東參政。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Shandong administrative commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through offices to administrative commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 撫綏流移，俸余悉給公用，帝聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: He pacified displaced populations and gave all his salary surplus to public use; the Emperor heard of it and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified displaced populations and gave all his salary surplus to public use; when the Emperor heard of it he praised him.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年，召為工部尚書，出為河南參政，歷浙江布政使，入為御史臺右大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongwu he was summoned as Minister of Works, then sent out as Henan administrative commissioner, served as Zhejiang provincial administration commissioner, and entered the capital as Right Censor of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 2 he was summoned as Minister of Works, then sent out as Henan administrative commissioner, served as Zhejiang provincial administration commissioner, and entered the capital as Right Censor of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 十三年改左中丞，坐事免。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief but was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was made Left Vice Censor-in-Chief but was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召為四輔官。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as one of the Four Assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned as one of the Four Assistants.

sentences.zh: 先是，胡惟庸謀反伏誅，帝以歷代丞相多擅權，遂罷中書省，分其職於六部。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Hu Weiyong's plot to rebel was exposed and he was executed, the Emperor, reflecting that chancellors of successive dynasties had often monopolized power, abolished the Secretariat and divided its duties among the Six Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Hu Weiyong's plot to rebel was exposed and he was executed, the Emperor, reflecting that chancellors of successive dynasties had often monopolized power, abolished the Secretariat and divided its duties among the Six Ministries.

sentences.zh: 既又念密勿論思不可無人，乃建四輔官，以四時為號，詔天下舉賢才。

translations.literal: He then reflected that confidential deliberation could not be left without men, and so established the office of the Four Assistants, titled after the four seasons, and ordered the realm to recommend worthy talent.
translations.idiomatic: He then reflected that confidential deliberation could not be left without men, and so established the office of the Four Assistants, titled after the four seasons, and ordered the realm to recommend worthy talent.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書範敏薦耆儒王本、杜佑、龔斅，杜斅、趙民望、吳源等。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Fan Min recommended veteran scholars Wang Ben, Du You, and Gong Xiao, and Gong Xiao, Zhao Minwang, Wu Yuan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Fan Min recommended veteran scholars Wang Ben, Du You, and Gong Xiao, along with Gong Xiao, Zhao Minwang, Wu Yuan, and others.

sentences.zh: 召至，告於太廟，以本、佑、龔斅為春官；

translations.literal: When they were summoned to court, the appointment was announced at the Imperial Ancestral Temple; Wang Ben, Du You, and Gong Xiao were made Spring Officials;
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, the appointment was announced at the Imperial Ancestral Temple: Wang Ben, Du You, and Gong Xiao were made Spring Officials;

sentences.zh: 杜斅、民望、源為夏官。

translations.literal: Du Xiao, Minwang, and Yuan were made Summer Officials.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiao, Minwang, and Yuan were made Summer Officials.

sentences.zh: 秋、冬闕，命本等攝之。

translations.literal: The Autumn and Winter posts were vacant, and Ben and the others were ordered to act in those capacities.
translations.idiomatic: The Autumn and Winter posts were left vacant, and Ben and the others were ordered to serve in those capacities as well.

sentences.zh: 位都督次，屢賜敕諭，隆以坐論之禮，命協贊政事，均調四時。

translations.literal: Their rank was next below regional commanders; they were repeatedly granted imperial rescripts, honored with the seated deliberation rite, ordered to assist in government affairs, and to harmonize the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: They ranked just below regional commanders, received repeated imperial rescripts, were honored with the seated deliberation rite, and were charged to assist in government and harmonize the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 會立冬，朔風釀寒。

translations.literal: It happened to be the beginning of winter, and the north wind brought cold.
translations.idiomatic: When winter began, the north wind brought cold.

sentences.zh: 帝以為順冬令，乃本等功，賜敕嘉勉。

translations.literal: The Emperor took this as conforming to the winter ordinance and as the achievement of Ben and the others, and granted a rescript of praise and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took this as conforming to the winter ordinance and as the achievement of Ben and his colleagues, and sent a rescript of praise.

sentences.zh: 又月分三旬，人各司之，以雨昜時若，驗其稱職與否。

translations.literal: Moreover the month was divided into three ten-day periods, each man taking charge of one, so that rain and sunshine might come in season, and their fitness for office could be tested.
translations.idiomatic: The month was also divided into three ten-day periods, each man taking one, so that rain and sunshine might come in season and their fitness for office could be tested.

sentences.zh: 刑官議獄，四輔及諫院覆核奏行，有疑讞，四輔官封駁。

translations.literal: When penal officials deliberated cases, the Four Assistants and the Remonstrance Bureau reviewed them and memorialized for action; in doubtful cases the Four Assistants sealed and returned the documents.
translations.idiomatic: When penal officials deliberated cases, the Four Assistants and the Remonstrance Bureau reviewed them before memorializing for action; in doubtful cases the Four Assistants returned the documents with objections.

sentences.zh: 居無何，斅等四人相繼致仕，召然代之。

translations.literal: Before long Xiao and the other four retired in succession, and Ran was summoned to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xiao and the other four retired in succession, and Ran was summoned to take their place.

sentences.zh: 本後坐事誅。

translations.literal: Ben was later executed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Ben was later executed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 諸人皆老儒，起田家，惇樸無他長。

translations.literal: All these men were elderly Confucians raised from farming families, honest and plain, without other special talents.
translations.idiomatic: All these men were elderly Confucians raised from farming families, honest and plain, without other special talents.

sentences.zh: 獨然久歷中外，練達庶務，眷註特隆。

translations.literal: Only Ran had long served both inside and outside the capital, was practiced in routine affairs, and received exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: Only Ran had long served both in the capital and in the provinces, was practiced in routine affairs, and received exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 十四年八月卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of the fourteenth year.

sentences.zh: 帝念然來歸之誠，親制文祭之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, mindful of Ran's sincerity in coming over to the Ming cause, personally composed a text to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Ran's sincerity in submitting to the Ming cause, the Emperor personally composed a sacrificial text for him.

sentences.zh: 繼然為四輔者，李幹、何顯周。

translations.literal: Those who succeeded Ran as Four Assistants were Li Gan and He Xianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Those who succeeded Ran as Four Assistants were Li Gan and He Xianzhou.

sentences.zh: 幹出為知府，佑、顯周俱罷去，是官遂廢不復設。

translations.literal: Gan was sent out as prefect; You and Xianzhou were both dismissed, and the office was then abolished and never re-established.
translations.idiomatic: Gan was sent out as prefect; You and Xianzhou were both dismissed, and the office was then abolished and never re-established.

sentences.zh: 本，不詳其籍裏。

translations.literal: Ben's native place is not recorded in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Ben's native place is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 佑，安邑人。

translations.literal: You was a native of Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: You came from Anyi.

sentences.zh: 嘗三主本布政司鄉試，稱得人。

translations.literal: He thrice served as chief examiner of the provincial civil examinations for the original provincial administration commission and was praised for selecting the right men.
translations.idiomatic: He thrice served as chief examiner of the provincial civil examinations and was praised for selecting the right men.

sentences.zh: 龔斅，鉛出人。

translations.literal: Gong Xiao was a native of Yanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Xiao came from Yanshan.

sentences.zh: 以行誼重於鄉。

translations.literal: He was esteemed in his home district for conduct and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He was esteemed in his home district for conduct and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 致仕後，復起為國子司業，歷祭酒。

translations.literal: After retirement he was recalled as vice director of the National University and rose to director.
translations.idiomatic: After retirement he was recalled as vice director of the National University and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 坐放諸生假不奏聞，免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for granting students leave without reporting it.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for granting students leave without reporting it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 杜斅，字致道，壺關人。

translations.literal: Du Xiao, style name Zhidao, was a native of Huguan.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiao, styled Zhidao, came from Huguan.

sentences.zh: 舉元鄉試第一，歷官臺州學正。

translations.literal: He placed first in the Yuan provincial examination and served as director of studies at Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He placed first in the Yuan provincial examination and served as director of studies at Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 歸家教授。

translations.literal: He returned home to teach.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to teach.

sentences.zh: 通《易》、《詩》、《書》三經。

translations.literal: He mastered the three classics: the 《Changes》, the 《Odes》, and the 《Documents》.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the three classics: the 《Changes》, the 《Odes》, and the 《Documents》.

sentences.zh: 源，莆田人。

translations.literal: Yuan was a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan came from Putian.

sentences.zh: 亦再征為國子司業，卒於官。

translations.literal: He too was twice summoned as vice director of the National University and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He too was twice summoned as vice director of the National University and died in office.

sentences.zh: 民望，槁城人。

translations.literal: Minwang was a native of Gaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Minwang came from Gaocheng.

sentences.zh: 幹，絳州人。

translations.literal: Gan was a native of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gan came from Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 顯周，內黃人。

translations.literal: Xianzhou was a native of Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhou came from Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 吳伯宗，名祐，以字行，金谿人。

translations.literal: Wu Bozong, given name You, was known by his style name and was a native of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Bozong, born You, went by his style name and came from Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年，廷試第一。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu he placed first in the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 4 he placed first in the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 時開科之始，帝親制策問。

translations.literal: It was the beginning of the civil examinations; the Emperor personally composed the policy questions.
translations.idiomatic: It was the beginning of the civil examinations, and the Emperor personally composed the policy questions.

sentences.zh: 得伯宗甚喜，賜冠帶袍笏，授禮部員外郎，與修《大明日歷》。

translations.literal: Delighted with Bozong, the Emperor bestowed cap, belt, robe, and tablet, appointed him vice director in the Ministry of Rites, and had him assist in compiling the 《Great Ming Calendar》.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted with Bozong, the Emperor bestowed cap, belt, robe, and tablet, appointed him vice director in the Ministry of Rites, and had him assist in compiling the 《Great Ming Calendar》.

sentences.zh: 胡惟庸用事，欲人附己，伯宗不為屈。

translations.literal: When Hu Weiyong held power he wanted men to attach themselves to him; Bozong would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Weiyong held power he wanted men to attach themselves to him, but Bozong would not yield.

sentences.zh: 惟庸銜之，坐事謫居鳳陽。

translations.literal: Weiyong bore a grudge and had him banished to Fengyang on a charge.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyong bore a grudge and had him banished to Fengyang on a charge.

sentences.zh: 上書論時政，因言惟庸專恣不法，不宜獨任，久之必為國患。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial on current affairs, saying that Weiyong was willful and lawless, unfit to hold power alone, and that in time he would surely become a peril to the state.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial on current affairs, saying that Weiyong was willful and lawless, unfit to hold power alone, and that in time he would surely become a peril to the state.

sentences.zh: 辭甚愷切。

translations.literal: His language was earnest and moving.
translations.idiomatic: His language was earnest and moving.

sentences.zh: 帝得奏，召還，賜衣鈔。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the memorial he summoned him back and bestowed clothing and paper money.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor received the memorial he summoned him back and bestowed clothing and paper money.

sentences.zh: 奉使安南，稱旨。

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to Annan, he pleased the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Sent as envoy to Annan, he pleased the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 除國子助教，命進講東宮。

translations.literal: He was appointed assistant tutor of the National University and ordered to lecture in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed assistant tutor of the National University and ordered to lecture in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 首陳正心誠意之說。

translations.literal: He first set forth the doctrine of rectifying the mind and making the will sincere.
translations.idiomatic: He first set forth the doctrine of rectifying the mind and making the will sincere.

sentences.zh: 改翰林典籍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin archivist.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hanlin archivist.

sentences.zh: 帝制十題命賦，援筆立就，詞旨雅潔。

translations.literal: The Emperor set ten topics and ordered rhapsodies; Bozong took up the brush and finished at once, his diction elegant and refined.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor set ten topics and ordered rhapsodies; Bozong took up the brush and finished at once, his diction elegant and refined.

sentences.zh: 賜織金錦衣。

translations.literal: He was granted a brocaded gold-thread robe.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a brocaded gold-thread robe.

sentences.zh: 除太常司丞，辭。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices but declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices but declined.

sentences.zh: 改國子司業，又辭。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the National University and again declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the National University and again declined.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，貶金縣教諭。

translations.literal: Having offended the imperial intent, he was demoted to instructor at Jin County.
translations.idiomatic: Having offended the Emperor, he was demoted to instructor at Jin County.

sentences.zh: 未至，詔還為翰林檢討。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, an edict recalled him as Hanlin compiling editor.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, an edict recalled him as Hanlin compiling editor.

sentences.zh: 十五年進武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to Grand Academician of the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to Grand Academician of the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，坐弟仲實為三河知縣薦舉不實，詞連伯宗，降檢討。

translations.literal: The next winter, because his younger brother Zhongshi as magistrate of Sanhe had made a false recommendation, the case implicated Bozong, and he was demoted to compiling editor.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter, because his younger brother Zhongshi as magistrate of Sanhe had made a false recommendation, the case implicated Bozong, and he was demoted to compiling editor.

sentences.zh: 伯宗為人溫厚，然內剛，不茍弇阿，故屢躓。

translations.literal: Bozong was mild in manner yet inwardly firm, unwilling to flatter or truckle, and therefore stumbled repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Bozong was mild in manner yet inwardly firm, unwilling to flatter or truckle, and therefore stumbled repeatedly in his career.

sentences.zh: 逾年，卒於官。

translations.literal: After a year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died in office.

sentences.zh: 伯宗成進士，考試官則宋濂、鮑恂也。

translations.literal: When Bozong became a presented scholar, his examiners were Song Lian and Bao Xun.
translations.idiomatic: When Bozong became a presented scholar, his examiners were Song Lian and Bao Xun.

sentences.zh: 恂，字仲孚，崇德人。

translations.literal: Xun, style name Zhongfu, was a native of Chongde.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xun, styled Zhongfu, came from Chongde.

sentences.zh: 受《易》於臨川吳澄。

translations.literal: He studied the 《Changes》 under Wu Cheng of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the 《Changes》 under Wu Cheng of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 好古力行，著《大易傳義》，學者稱之。

translations.literal: He loved antiquity and practiced earnestly, authored the 《Exegesis of the Great Changes》, and scholars praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved antiquity and practiced earnestly, authored the 《Exegesis of the Great Changes》, and scholars praised him.

sentences.zh: 元至正中，以薦授溫州路學正。

translations.literal: In the Zhizheng reign of the Yuan he was recommended and appointed director of studies on the Wenzhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhizheng reign of the Yuan he was recommended and appointed director of studies on the Wenzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 尋召入翰林，不就。

translations.literal: Soon summoned to the Hanlin Academy, he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Soon summoned to the Hanlin Academy, he declined.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年，初科舉取士，召為同考官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu, at the first civil examination for selecting scholars, he was summoned as co-examiner.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 4, at the first civil examination for selecting scholars, he was summoned as co-examiner.

sentences.zh: 試已，辭去。

translations.literal: When the examination was over he resigned and left.
translations.idiomatic: When the examination was over he resigned and left.

sentences.zh: 十五年與吉安余詮、高郵張長年、登州張紳，皆以明經老成為禮部主事劉庸所薦，召至京。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he, together with Yu Quan of Ji'an, Zhang Changnian of Gaoyou, and Zhang Shen of Dengzhou—all elderly masters of the classics recommended by Liu Yong, a director in the Ministry of Rites—was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he, together with Yu Quan of Ji'an, Zhang Changnian of Gaoyou, and Zhang Shen of Dengzhou—all elderly masters of the classics recommended by Liu Yong of the Ministry of Rites—was summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 恂年八十余，長年、詮亦皆逾七十矣。

translations.literal: Xun was over eighty; Changnian and Quan were also past seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was over eighty; Changnian and Quan were also past seventy.

sentences.zh: 賜坐顧問。

translations.literal: They were granted seats and consulted.
translations.idiomatic: They were granted seats and consulted.

sentences.zh: 翌日並命為文華殿大學士，皆以老疾固辭，遂放還。

translations.literal: The next day all were appointed Grand Academicians of the Wenhua Hall; all firmly declined on grounds of age and illness, and were sent home.
translations.idiomatic: The next day all were appointed Grand Academicians of the Wenhua Hall; all firmly declined on grounds of age and illness and were sent home.

sentences.zh: 紳後至，以為鄠縣教諭，尋召為右僉都御史，終浙江左布政使。

translations.literal: Shen arrived later, was made instructor of Hu County, soon summoned as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, and ended as Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen arrived later, was made instructor of Hu County, was soon summoned as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, and ended as Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 其明年以耆儒征者，曰全思誠，字希賢，上海人，亦授文華殿大學士。

translations.literal: The next year another elderly scholar was summoned: Quan Sicheng, style name Xixian, a native of Shanghai, who was also appointed Grand Academician of the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The next year another elderly scholar was summoned: Quan Sicheng, styled Xixian, from Shanghai, who was also appointed Grand Academician of the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 又明年請老，賜敕致仕。

translations.literal: The year after that he asked to retire on account of age and was granted an edict of retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he asked to retire on account of age and was granted an edict of retirement.

sentences.zh: 伯宗之使安南也，以名德為交人所重。

translations.literal: When Bozong was envoy to Annan, the people of Jiaozhi esteemed him for his reputation and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When Bozong served as envoy to Annan, the people of Jiaozhi esteemed him for his reputation and virtue.

sentences.zh: 其後，襄陽任亨泰亦舉洪武二十一年進士第一，以禮部尚書使安南，交人以為榮。

translations.literal: Later Ren Hengtai of Xiangyang also placed first among presented scholars in the twenty-first year of Hongwu and, as Minister of Rites, was envoy to Annan; the people of Jiaozhi took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ren Hengtai of Xiangyang also placed first among presented scholars in Hongwu 21 and, as Minister of Rites, was envoy to Annan; the people of Jiaozhi took it as an honor.

sentences.zh: 前後使安南者，並稱吳、任雲。

translations.literal: Envoys to Annan before and after were all styled "the clouds of Wu and Ren."
translations.idiomatic: Envoys to Annan before and after were all styled "the clouds of Wu and Ren."

sentences.zh: 亨泰為禮部尚書時，日照民江伯兒以母病殺其三歲子祀岱嶽。

translations.literal: When Hengtai was Minister of Rites, Jiang Bo'er of Rizhao killed his three-year-old son to sacrifice to Mount Tai because his mother was ill.
translations.idiomatic: When Hengtai was Minister of Rites, Jiang Bo'er of Rizhao killed his three-year-old son to sacrifice to Mount Tai because his mother was ill.

sentences.zh: 有司以聞。

translations.literal: The local officials reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The local officials reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝怒其滅絕倫理，杖百，戍海南。

translations.literal: The Emperor, enraged at this extinction of human relations, had him beaten one hundred strokes and exiled to guard Hainan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, enraged at this violation of human relations, had him beaten one hundred strokes and exiled to Hainan.

sentences.zh: 因命亨泰定旌表孝行事例。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered Hengtai to fix regulations for honoring filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered Hengtai to fix regulations for honoring filial conduct.

sentences.zh: 亨泰議曰：「人子事親，居則致其敬，養則致其樂，有疾則謹其醫藥。

translations.literal: Hengtai proposed: "A son serving his parents should show respect in daily life, give joy in nurturing them, and be careful with medicine when they are ill.
translations.idiomatic: Hengtai proposed, "A son serving his parents should show respect in daily life, give joy in nurturing them, and be careful with medicine when they are ill.

sentences.zh: 臥冰割股，事非恒經。

translations.literal: Lying on ice or cutting flesh from one's thigh are not constant norms.
translations.idiomatic: Lying on ice or cutting flesh from one's thigh are not established norms.

sentences.zh: 割股不已，致於割肝，割肝不已，至於殺子。

translations.literal: Cutting the thigh without stopping leads to cutting the liver; cutting the liver without stopping leads to killing one's child.
translations.idiomatic: Cutting the thigh without stopping leads to cutting the liver; cutting the liver without stopping leads to killing one's child.

sentences.zh: 違道傷生，莫此為甚。

translations.literal: To violate the Way and harm life—nothing is worse than this.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing violates the Way and harms life more than this.

sentences.zh: 墮宗絕祀，尤不孝之大者，宜嚴行戒諭。

translations.literal: To destroy one's lineage and cut off sacrifice is the greatest of unfilial acts; strict warnings should be issued.
translations.idiomatic: To destroy one's lineage and cut off sacrifice is the greatest of unfilial acts; strict warnings should be issued.

sentences.zh: 倘愚昧無知，亦聽其所為，不在旌表之例。」

translations.literal: If men are foolish and ignorant, let them do as they will; such cases are not within the scope of public honor."
translations.idiomatic: If men are foolish and ignorant, let them do as they will; such cases are not to receive public honors."

sentences.zh: 詔曰「可」。

translations.literal: An edict said "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Approved."

sentences.zh: 明年，議秦王喪禮，因定凡世子襲爵之禮。

translations.literal: The next year, deliberating the mourning rites for the Prince of Qin, he thereby fixed the rites for heirs apparent inheriting noble rank in general.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, while deliberating the mourning rites for the Prince of Qin, he fixed the rites for heirs apparent inheriting noble rank in general.

sentences.zh: 會討龍州趙宗壽，命偕御史嚴震直使安南，諭以謹邊方，無納逋逃。

translations.literal: When the court was discussing Zhao Zongshou of Longzhou, he was ordered together with Censor Yan Zhenzhi to go as envoy to Annan, instructing them to guard the frontier carefully and not harbor fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was discussing Zhao Zongshou of Longzhou, he was ordered together with Censor Yan Zhenzhi to go as envoy to Annan, instructing them to guard the frontier carefully and not harbor fugitives.

sentences.zh: 時帝以安南篡弒，絕其貢使。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor, because Annan had usurped and murdered its ruler, had cut off its tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Emperor, because Annan had usurped and murdered its ruler, had cut off its tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 至是聞詔使至，震恐。

translations.literal: When they now heard that imperial envoys had arrived, they were terrified.
translations.idiomatic: When they now heard that imperial envoys had arrived, they were terrified.

sentences.zh: 亨泰為書，述朝廷用兵之故以安慰之，交人大悅。

translations.literal: Hengtai wrote a letter explaining why the court had used troops, to reassure them; the people of Jiaozhi were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Hengtai wrote a letter explaining why the court had used troops, to reassure them; the people of Jiaozhi were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 使還，以私市蠻人為仆，降御史。

translations.literal: On his return from the mission he was demoted to censor for privately purchasing barbarians as servants.
translations.idiomatic: On his return from the mission he was demoted to censor for privately purchasing barbarians as servants.

sentences.zh: 未幾，思明土官與安南爭界，詞復連亨泰，坐免官。

translations.literal: Before long the native official of Siming disputed the border with Annan; the case again implicated Hengtai, and he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the native official of Siming disputed the border with Annan; the case again implicated Hengtai, and he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 吳沈，字浚仲，蘭溪人。

translations.literal: Wu Chen, style name Junzhong, was a native of Lanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chen, styled Junzhong, came from Lanxi.

sentences.zh: 元國子博士師道子也，以學行聞。

translations.literal: He was the son of Shidao, erudite of the Yuan National University, and was known for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of Shidao, erudite of the Yuan National University, and was known for learning and conduct.

sentences.zh: 太祖下婺州，召沈及同郡許元、葉瓚玉、胡翰、汪仲山、李公常、金信、徐孳、童冀、戴良、吳履、孫履、張起敬會食省中，日令二人進講經史。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor took Wuzhou, he summoned Chen together with fellow townsman Xu Yuan, Ye Zanyu, Hu Han, Wang Zhongshan, Li Gongchang, Jin Xin, Xu Zi, Tong Ji, Dai Liang, Wu Lü, Sun Lü, and Zhang Qijing to dine in the provincial office, ordering two men each day to lecture on the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor took Wuzhou, he summoned Chen together with Xu Yuan, Ye Zanyu, Hu Han, Wang Zhongshan, Li Gongchang, Jin Xin, Xu Zi, Tong Ji, Dai Liang, Wu Lü, Sun Lü, and Zhang Qijing of the same commandery to dine in the provincial office, ordering two men each day to lecture on the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 已，命沈為郡學訓導。

translations.literal: Later he appointed Chen instructor of the prefectural school.
translations.idiomatic: Later he appointed Chen instructor of the prefectural school.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，郡以儒士舉，誤上其名曰信仲，授翰林院待制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu the prefecture recommended him as a Confucian scholar; his name was mistakenly submitted as Xinzhong, and he was appointed Hanlin awaiting edict.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongwu the prefecture recommended him as a Confucian scholar; his name was mistakenly submitted as Xinzhong, and he was appointed Hanlin awaiting edict.

sentences.zh: 沈謂修撰王厘曰：「名誤不更，是欺罔也。」

translations.literal: Chen said to reviser Wang Li: "If the name is wrong and is not corrected, that is deception."
translations.idiomatic: Chen said to reviser Wang Li, "If the name is wrong and is not corrected, that is deception."

sentences.zh: 將白於朝。

translations.literal: He was about to report it to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to report it to the court.

sentences.zh: 厘言：「恐觸上怒」。

translations.literal: Li said: "I fear it may provoke the Emperor's anger."
translations.idiomatic: Li said, "I fear it may provoke the Emperor's anger."

sentences.zh: 沈不從，牒請改正。

translations.literal: Chen would not agree and submitted a formal request for correction.
translations.idiomatic: Chen would not agree and submitted a formal request for correction.

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「誠愨人也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and said: "He is truly a sincere and honest man."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased and said, "He is truly a sincere and upright man."

sentences.zh: 遂眷遇之，召侍左右。

translations.literal: Thereupon he treated him with special favor and summoned him to attend at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Emperor treated him with special favor and summoned him to serve at his side.

sentences.zh: 以事降編修。

translations.literal: Because of an affair he was demoted to compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Over some matter he was demoted to compiler.

sentences.zh: 給事中鄭相同言：「故事啟事東宮，惟東宮官屬稱臣，朝臣則否。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Zheng Xiangtong said: "By precedent, when presenting matters to the Eastern Palace, only Eastern Palace officials called themselves 'subject'; court officials did not.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Zheng Xiangtong said, "By precedent, when reporting affairs to the Eastern Palace, only Eastern Palace officials styled themselves 'your subject'; court officials did not.

sentences.zh: 今一體稱臣，於禮未安。」

translations.literal: Now all alike call themselves 'subject'; this is not proper in ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Now everyone alike calls himself 'your subject'; in ritual terms this is improper."

sentences.zh: 沈駁之曰：「東宮，國之大本。

translations.literal: Chen rebutted him, saying: "The Eastern Palace is the great foundation of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Chen rebutted him, saying, "The Eastern Palace is the great foundation of the state.

sentences.zh: 尊東宮，所以尊主上也。

translations.literal: To honor the Eastern Palace is to honor the sovereign above.
translations.idiomatic: To honor the Eastern Palace is to honor the ruler above.

sentences.zh: 相同言非是。」

translations.literal: Xiangtong's words are not correct."
translations.idiomatic: What Xiangtong said is wrong."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sided with him.

sentences.zh: 尋以奏對失旨，降翰林院典籍。

translations.literal: Before long, because his responses at audience failed to satisfy the Emperor's intent, he was demoted to Hanlin Academy archivist.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, because his answers at audience missed the Emperor's intent, he was demoted to Hanlin Academy archivist.

sentences.zh: 已，擢東閣大學士。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 初，帝謂沈曰：「聖賢立教有三：曰敬天，曰忠君，曰孝親。

translations.literal: Initially the Emperor said to Chen: "The sages and worthies established teaching in three parts: revering Heaven, being loyal to the ruler, and being filial to parents.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Emperor had said to Chen, "The sages established teaching in three matters: reverence for Heaven, loyalty to the ruler, and filial devotion to parents.

sentences.zh: 散在經卷，未易會其要領。

translations.literal: These are scattered through the classics; it is not easy to grasp their essentials.
translations.idiomatic: They are scattered through the classics and not easy to grasp in their essentials.

sentences.zh: 爾等以三事編輯。」

translations.literal: You shall compile and edit them according to these three matters."
translations.idiomatic: You are to compile and edit them around these three themes."

sentences.zh: 至是書成，賜名《精誠錄》，命沈撰序。

translations.literal: By this time the book was completed; it was granted the name 《Record of Sincerity》, and Chen was ordered to compose the preface.
translations.idiomatic: By then the work was finished. It was given the title 《Record of Sincerity》, and Chen was ordered to write the preface.

sentences.zh: 居一年，降翰林侍書，改國子博士，以老歸。

translations.literal: After a year he was demoted to Hanlin attendant scribe, transferred to erudite of the National University, and returned home on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was demoted to Hanlin attendant scribe, reassigned as erudite of the National University, and retired home because of old age.

sentences.zh: 沈嘗著辯，言「孔子封王為非禮」。

translations.literal: Chen once wrote a disputation stating that "enfeoffing Confucius as a king was contrary to ritual propriety."
translations.idiomatic: Chen once wrote a disputation arguing that "enfeoffing Confucius as a king was not in accord with ritual propriety."

sentences.zh: 後布政使夏寅、祭酒丘浚皆沿其說。

translations.literal: Later provincial administration commissioner Xia Yin and chancellor of the National University Qiu Jun both followed his argument.
translations.idiomatic: Later provincial administration commissioner Xia Yin and chancellor of the National University Qiu Jun both adopted his view.

sentences.zh: 至嘉靖九年，更定祀典，改稱「至聖先師」，實自沈發之也。

translations.literal: By the ninth year of Jiajing the sacrificial statutes were revised and the title changed to "Most Sage-like First Teacher"; this in fact originated with Chen.
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth year of Jiajing the sacrificial canon was revised and the title changed to "Most Sage-like First Teacher"—a change that in fact began with Chen.

sentences.zh: 桂彥良，名德偁，以字行，慈谿人。

translations.literal: Gui Yanliang, personal name Decheng, was known by his style name; he was a native of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Yanliang, whose personal name was Decheng, went by his style name; he came from Cixi.

sentences.zh: 元鄉貢進士，為平江路學教授，罷歸。

translations.literal: Under the Yuan he was a metropolitan graduate via provincial recommendation, served as professor of the Pingjiang Route school, and was dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan he passed the metropolitan examination as a provincial nominee, served as professor of the Pingjiang Route school, and was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 張士誠、方國珍交辟，不就。

translations.literal: Zhang Shicheng and Fang Guozhen repeatedly summoned him; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng and Fang Guozhen both repeatedly invited him to serve; he refused.

sentences.zh: 洪武六年，征詣公車，授太子正字。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongwu he was summoned to the capital by imperial carriage and appointed Chief Rectifier of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Hongwu he was summoned to court and appointed Chief Rectifier to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗出禦制詩文，彥良就禦座前朗誦，聲徹殿外，左右驚愕，帝嘉其樸直。

translations.literal: The Emperor once produced his personally composed poetry and prose; Yanliang read them aloud before the imperial seat; his voice reached outside the hall; those at left and right were startled; the Emperor praised his plainspoken honesty.
translations.idiomatic: Once when the Emperor produced his own poetry and prose, Yanliang read them aloud before the throne until his voice carried outside the hall. Those standing by were astonished, and the Emperor praised his plain, straightforward manner.

sentences.zh: 時選國子生蔣學等為給事中，舉人張唯等為編修，肄業文華堂。

translations.literal: At that time selected National University students such as Jiang Xue were made supervising secretaries, and presented scholars such as Zhang Wei were made compilers, studying at the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At that time selected National University students such as Jiang Xue were appointed supervising secretaries, and presented scholars such as Zhang Wei were appointed compilers to study at the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 命彥良及宋濂、孔克表為之師。

translations.literal: Yanliang together with Song Lian and Kong Kebiao were appointed their teachers.
translations.idiomatic: Yanliang, Song Lian, and Kong Kebiao were appointed to teach them.

sentences.zh: 嘗從容有所咨問，彥良對必以正。

translations.literal: When the Emperor casually inquired about something, Yanliang always answered uprightly.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor casually questioned him, Yanliang always answered with rectitude.

sentences.zh: 帝每稱善，書其語揭便殿。

translations.literal: The Emperor often expressed approval and had his words written out and displayed in the side hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor often praised him and had his words written out and posted in the side hall.

sentences.zh: 七年冬至，詞臣撰南郊祝文用「予」、「我」字。

translations.literal: On the Winter Solstice of the seventh year, the literary officials drafted the southern suburban sacrificial prayer using the characters "yu" and "wo" for "I."
translations.idiomatic: On the Winter Solstice of the seventh year, the literary officials drafted the southern suburban prayer using the first-person pronouns "yu" and "wo."

sentences.zh: 帝以為不敬。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered this disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor regarded this as disrespectful.

sentences.zh: 彥良曰：「成湯祭上帝曰『予小子履』；

translations.literal: Yanliang said: "When Cheng Tang sacrificed to Shangdi he said, 'I, the little child Lu';
translations.idiomatic: Yanliang said, "When Cheng Tang sacrificed to the Supreme Lord he said, 'I, the little child Lu';

sentences.zh: 武王祀文王之詩曰「『我將我享』。

translations.literal: the poem on King Wu's sacrifice to King Wen says, "'I bring and I offer.
translations.idiomatic: and in the poem on King Wu's sacrifice to King Wen it says, "'I bring and I offer.

sentences.zh: 古有此言。」

translations.literal: Ancient times had such language."
translations.idiomatic: Such language existed in antiquity."

sentences.zh: 帝色霽曰：「正字言是也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor's countenance cleared and he said: "The Chief Rectifier speaks correctly."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's expression cleared and he said, "The Chief Rectifier is right."

sentences.zh: 時御史臺具獄，令詞臣覆讞。

translations.literal: At that time the Censorate prepared cases and ordered the literary officials to review the verdicts.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Censorate prepared cases and ordered the literary officials to review the judgments.

sentences.zh: 彥良所論釋者數十人。

translations.literal: Several dozen people were released through Yanliang's deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen people were released through Yanliang's review.

sentences.zh: 遷晉王府右傅。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Tutor of the Prince of Jin's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Tutor in the Prince of Jin's household.

sentences.zh: 帝親為文賜之。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally composed a text and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor personally wrote an essay and bestowed it on him.

sentences.zh: 彥良入謝。

translations.literal: Yanliang entered to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Yanliang went in to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「江南大儒，惟卿一人。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Among the great Confucians of Jiangnan, you alone remain."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Among the great Confucians of Jiangnan, you alone remain."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣不如宋濂、劉基。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject is not the equal of Song Lian and Liu Ji."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your subject is not the equal of Song Lian and Liu Ji."

sentences.zh: 帝曰「濂，文人耳；

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Lian is merely a man of letters;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Lian is only a man of letters;

sentences.zh: 基，峻隘，不如卿也。」

translations.literal: Ji is stern and narrow-minded — he is not your equal."
translations.idiomatic: Ji is harsh and narrow-minded. He is not your equal."

sentences.zh: 彥良至晉，制《格心圖》獻王。

translations.literal: When Yanliang reached Jin, he composed the 《Chart for Rectifying the Mind》 and presented it to the prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanliang reached Jin, he composed the 《Chart for Rectifying the Mind》 and presented it to the prince.

sentences.zh: 後更王府官制，改左長史。

translations.literal: Later when the princely establishment offices were reorganized, he was changed to Left Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the princely establishment offices were reorganized, he was reassigned as Left Chief Secretary.

sentences.zh: 朝京師，上太平十二策。

translations.literal: On an audience at the capital he submitted Twelve Policies for Peace.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court at the capital he submitted Twelve Policies for Peace.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「彥良所陳，通達事體，有裨治道。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "What Yanliang has set forth comprehends the substance of affairs and benefits the way of governance.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "What Yanliang has set forth understands the substance of affairs and aids the way of governance.

sentences.zh: 世謂儒者泥古不通今，若彥良可謂通儒矣。」

translations.literal: The world says Confucians cling to antiquity and do not understand the present; a man like Yanliang may be called a comprehensive Confucian."
translations.idiomatic: People say Confucians cling to antiquity and cannot grasp the present, but a man like Yanliang may truly be called a comprehensive Confucian."

sentences.zh: 十八年請告歸，越二年卒。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he requested leave to return home; two years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he requested leave to return home; two years later he died.

sentences.zh: 明初，特重師傅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ming, tutors were especially valued.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Ming, tutors were especially esteemed.

sentences.zh: 既命宋濂教太子，而諸王傅亦慎其選。

translations.literal: Once Song Lian was appointed to teach the Heir Apparent, the tutors of the various princes were also chosen with care.
translations.idiomatic: After Song Lian was appointed to teach the Heir Apparent, the tutors of the various princes were also chosen with great care.

sentences.zh: 彥良與陳南賓等皆宿儒老生，而李希顏與駙馬都尉胡觀傅徐宗實，尤以嚴見憚。

translations.literal: Yanliang and Chen Nanbin and others were all elderly Confucians of long standing, while Li Xiyan and Xu Zongshi, tutor to imperial son-in-law commandant Hu Guan, were especially feared for their sternness.
translations.idiomatic: Yanliang, Chen Nanbin, and others were all venerable old scholars, while Li Xiyan and Xu Zongshi, tutor to Hu Guan, Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-law's Establishment, were especially feared for their severity.

sentences.zh: 李希顏，字愚庵，郟人。

translations.literal: Li Xiyan, style name Yuan'an, was a native of Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiyan, styled Yuan'an, came from Jia.

sentences.zh: 隱居不仕。

translations.literal: He lived in seclusion and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in seclusion and refused office.

sentences.zh: 太祖手書徵之，至京，為諸王師。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor personally wrote to summon him; when he reached the capital he became teacher to the princes.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor summoned him with a letter in his own hand; when he reached the capital he became tutor to the princes.

sentences.zh: 規範嚴峻，諸王有不率教者，或擊其額。

translations.literal: His standards were stern and severe; when princes did not follow his instruction, he would sometimes strike them on the forehead.
translations.idiomatic: His discipline was stern and severe; when princes failed to follow his teaching, he would sometimes strike them on the forehead.

sentences.zh: 帝撫而怒。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and consoled the princes.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was angry and comforted the princes.

sentences.zh: 高皇后曰：「烏有以聖人之道訓吾子，顧怒之耶？」

translations.literal: Empress Gao said: "How could there be one who instructs our sons in the Way of the sages, yet you are angry with him?"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Gao said, "Can there be one who teaches our sons the Way of the sages, and yet you are angry with him?"

sentences.zh: 太祖意解，授左春坊右贊善。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor's anger eased; he was appointed Right Supporter of the Left Spring Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor's anger eased, and Xiyan was appointed Right Supporter of the Left Spring Office.

sentences.zh: 諸王就藩，希顏歸舊隱。

translations.literal: When the princes took up their fiefs, Xiyan returned to his former seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: When the princes went to their fiefs, Xiyan returned to his former retirement.

sentences.zh: 閭裏宴集，常著緋袍戴笠往。

translations.literal: At neighborhood banquets he often wore a crimson robe and went wearing a bamboo hat.
translations.idiomatic: At neighborhood gatherings he often wore a crimson robe and a bamboo hat.

sentences.zh: 客問故，笑曰：「笠本質，緋，君賜也。」

translations.literal: When guests asked the reason, he smiled and said: "The hat is my natural self; the crimson is the ruler's gift."
translations.idiomatic: When guests asked why, he smiled and said, "The hat is my natural self; the crimson is the ruler's gift."

sentences.zh: 徐宗實，名垕，以字行，黃巖人。

translations.literal: Xu Zongshi, personal name Hou, was known by his style name; he was a native of Huangyan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zongshi, whose personal name was Hou, went by his style name; he came from Huangyan.

sentences.zh: 少穎悟。

translations.literal: From youth he was keen and quick-witted.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was quick and perceptive.

sentences.zh: 篤於學。

translations.literal: He was devoted to learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply devoted to study.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，被薦，除銅陵簿。

translations.literal: During Hongwu he was recommended and appointed recorder of Tongling.
translations.idiomatic: During Hongwu he was recommended and appointed clerk of Tongling.

sentences.zh: 請告迎養，忤帝意，謫戍淮陰驛。

translations.literal: When he requested leave to go home and care for his parents, he offended the Emperor's intent and was banished to serve at the Huaiyin post station.
translations.idiomatic: When he requested leave to go home and support his parents, he offended the Emperor and was banished to serve at the Huaiyin post station.

sentences.zh: 會東川侯胡海子觀選尚主，帝為觀擇師，難其人，以命宗實。

translations.literal: It happened that Hu Guan, son of Marquis Hu of Dongchuan, was selected to marry an imperial princess; the Emperor sought a tutor for Guan but found it hard to choose someone suitable, and assigned Zongshi.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Hu Guan, son of Marquis Hu of Dongchuan, was chosen to marry an imperial princess. The Emperor sought a tutor for Guan but found no suitable candidate, and so appointed Zongshi.

sentences.zh: 中使援他府例，置駙馬位中堂南向，而布師席於西階上東向。

translations.literal: A palace envoy cited the precedent of other establishments, placing the imperial son-in-law's seat in the central hall facing south, with the teacher's mat laid on the western steps facing east.
translations.idiomatic: A palace envoy cited the precedent of other households, placing the imperial son-in-law's seat in the central hall facing south and laying the teacher's mat on the western steps facing east.

sentences.zh: 宗實手引駙馬位使下，然後為說書。

translations.literal: Zongshi took the imperial son-in-law by the hand and led him down from the seat, and only then lectured.
translations.idiomatic: Zongshi took the imperial son-in-law by the hand and led him down from the seat, and only then began his lecture.

sentences.zh: 左右大驚，相顧以目。

translations.literal: Those left and right were greatly startled and exchanged glances.
translations.idiomatic: Those standing by were greatly startled and exchanged glances.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而嘉之，召宗實慰勞數四。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard he commended him and summoned Zongshi several times to express consolation and commendation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard of it he praised him and summoned Zongshi several times to comfort and commend him.

sentences.zh: 陳南賓，名光裕，以字行，茶陵人。

translations.literal: Chen Nanbin, personal name Guangyu, was known by his style name; he was a native of Chaling.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Nanbin, whose personal name was Guangyu, went by his style name; he came from Chaling.

sentences.zh: 元末為全州學正。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan he was director of studies of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan he served as director of studies in Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，聘至都，除無棣丞，歷膠州同知，所至以經術為治。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was invited to the capital and appointed assistant magistrate of Wudi; he served successively as vice prefect of Jiaozhou; wherever he went he governed through classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongwu he was invited to the capital and appointed assistant magistrate of Wudi, then served as vice prefect of Jiaozhou; wherever he went he governed through classical learning.

sentences.zh: 召為國子助教。

translations.literal: He was summoned as assistant instructor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as assistant instructor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 嘗入見，講《洪範》九疇。

translations.literal: On one occasion he had an audience and expounded the Nine Categories of the 《Hongfan》.
translations.idiomatic: On one audience he expounded the 《Hongfan》 Nine Categories.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，書姓名殿柱。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and wrote his name on a hall pillar.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly pleased and wrote his name on a hall pillar.

sentences.zh: 後禦註《洪範》，多采其說。

translations.literal: Later when the Emperor personally annotated the 《Hongfan》, he largely adopted his explanations.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Emperor personally annotated the 《Hongfan》, he largely adopted Nanbin's explanations.

sentences.zh: 擢蜀府長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Chief Secretary of the Prince of Shu's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Chief Secretary of the Prince of Shu's household.

sentences.zh: 蜀獻王好學，敬禮尤至，造安車以賜，為構第，名「安老堂。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Shu was fond of learning and showed him exceptional courtesy and respect; he had a comfortable carriage made and bestowed it, and built a residence for him named "Hall of Peaceful Old Age."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shu loved learning and showed him exceptional respect. He had a comfortable carriage made and bestowed it on him, and built a residence for him named "Hall of Peaceful Old Age."

sentences.zh: 二十九年，與方孝孺同為四川考試官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he served together with Fang Xiaoru as examination official for Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he served with Fang Xiaoru as examination official for Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 詩文清勁有法。

translations.literal: His poetry and prose were clear, forceful, and disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose were clear, forceful, and well ordered.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 其後諸王府長史劉淳、董子莊、趙季通、楊黼、金實、蕭用道、宋子環之屬，皆有名。

translations.literal: Afterward chief secretaries of various princely establishments such as Liu Chun, Dong Zizhuang, Zhao Jitong, Yang Fu, Jin Shi, Xiao Yongdao, Song Zihuan, and others all had reputations.
translations.idiomatic: After them, chief secretaries of various princely establishments such as Liu Chun, Dong Zizhuang, Zhao Jitong, Yang Fu, Jin Shi, Xiao Yongdao, Song Zihuan, and others all won renown.

sentences.zh: 劉淳，南陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Chun was a native of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chun came from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 洪武末為原武訓導。

translations.literal: At the end of Hongwu he was instructor of Yuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Hongwu he served as instructor of Yuanwu.

sentences.zh: 周王聘為世子師。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhou invited him as tutor to the heir.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Zhou invited him to serve as tutor to the heir.

sentences.zh: 尋言於朝，補右長史，以正輔王。

translations.literal: Before long he reported to the court and was appointed Right Chief Secretary to assist the prince with rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he reported to the court and was appointed Right Chief Secretary to assist the prince with rectitude.

sentences.zh: 端禮門槐盛夏而枯。

translations.literal: A pagoda tree at the Gate of Correct Ritual withered in midsummer.
translations.idiomatic: A pagoda tree at the Gate of Correct Ritual withered in midsummer.

sentences.zh: 淳陳咎徵進戒。

translations.literal: Chun presented it as an omen of blame and offered admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Chun cited it as an inauspicious sign and offered admonition.

sentences.zh: 王用其言修省，枯枝復榮。

translations.literal: The prince followed his advice in self-examination, and the withered branches flourished again.
translations.idiomatic: The prince followed his counsel in self-examination, and the withered branches flourished again.

sentences.zh: 王旌其槐曰「攄忠」。

translations.literal: The prince honored the tree with the inscription "Expressing Loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: The prince honored the tree with the inscription "Expressing Loyalty."

sentences.zh: 致仕十余年而卒，年九十有七。

translations.literal: More than ten years after retiring from office he died, aged ninety-seven.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years after retiring from office he died at the age of ninety-seven.

sentences.zh: 董子莊，名琰，以字行，江西樂安人。

translations.literal: Dong Zizhuang, personal name Yan, was known by his style name; he was a native of Le'an in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zizhuang, whose personal name was Yan, went by his style name; he came from Le'an in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 有學行。

translations.literal: He possessed learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of learning and integrity.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，以學官遷知茂名縣。

translations.literal: During Hongwu he was transferred from school official to magistrate of Maoming County.
translations.idiomatic: During Hongwu he was transferred from school official to magistrate of Maoming County.

sentences.zh: 永樂時，由國子司業出為趙王府右長史，隨事匡正。

translations.literal: During Yongle he went out from Vice Chancellor of the National University to become Right Chief Secretary of the Prince of Zhao's establishment, correcting matters as they arose.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongle he left his post as Vice Chancellor of the National University to become Right Chief Secretary of the Prince of Zhao's household, correcting affairs as they arose.

sentences.zh: 王多過，帝輒以責長史。

translations.literal: When the prince had many faults, the Emperor would hold the chief secretary accountable.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince committed many faults, the Emperor would hold the chief secretary responsible.

sentences.zh: 子莊以能諫，得無過。

translations.literal: Because Zizhuang was able to remonstrate, he incurred no fault.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zizhuang was able to remonstrate effectively, he incurred no blame.

sentences.zh: 十八年春當陪祀國社，夙起，衣冠端坐而卒。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighteenth year, when he was to accompany the sacrifice to the state altars of soil and grain, he rose early, dressed in cap and robes, sat upright, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighteenth year, when he was to attend the sacrifice at the state altars of soil and grain, he rose early, put on his cap and robes, sat upright, and died.

sentences.zh: 趙季通，字師道，天臺人。

translations.literal: Zhao Jitong, style name Shidao, was a native of Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jitong, whose style name was Shidao, came from Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 亦由教官歷知永豐、龍溪，與修《太祖實錄》，累進司業。

translations.literal: He too rose from school instructor through posts as magistrate of Yongfeng and Longxi, helped compile the 《Veritable Records of Taizu》, and was promoted repeatedly to Vice Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He too advanced from school instructor through appointments as magistrate of Yongfeng and Longxi, took part in compiling the 《Veritable Records of Taizu》, and was promoted step by step to Vice Chancellor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 出為趙王府左長史，與子莊同心輔導，藩府賢僚首稱趙、董雲。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Left Chief Secretary of the Prince of Zhao's establishment; working in concert with Zizhuang in guidance and instruction, Zhao and Dong were said to be foremost among the worthy officials of the princely household.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Left Chief Secretary of the Prince of Zhao's household and, working in concert with Zizhuang to guide and instruct the prince, he and Dong were regarded as the foremost worthy officials in the establishment.

sentences.zh: 金實，開化人。

translations.literal: Jin Shi was a native of Kaihua.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Shi came from Kaihua.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，上書言治道。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle he submitted a memorial on the way of governance.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yongle reign he submitted a memorial on the principles of good government.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 復對策，稱旨，除翰林典籍。

translations.literal: He again answered policy questions, pleased the throne, and was appointed Hanlin Archivist.
translations.idiomatic: He again answered policy questions to the Emperor's satisfaction and was appointed Hanlin Archivist.

sentences.zh: 與修《太祖實錄》、《永樂大典》，選為東宮講官。
