translations.literal: He helped compile the 《Veritable Records of Taizu》 and the 《Yongle Encyclopedia》, and was selected as a lecturer in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in compiling the 《Veritable Records of Taizu》 and the 《Yongle Encyclopedia》 and was chosen as a lecturer to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 歷左春坊左司直。

translations.literal: He served successively as Left Rectifier of the Left Secretariat of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Left Rectifier in the Left Secretariat of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 仁宗立，除衛府左長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong acceded, he was appointed Left Chief Secretary of the Prince of Wei's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong came to the throne, he was appointed Left Chief Secretary of the Prince of Wei's household.

sentences.zh: 正統初，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengtong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the beginning of the Zhengtong reign.

sentences.zh: 為人孝友，敦行誼。

translations.literal: As a man he was filial and fraternal, and earnest in friendship and duty.
translations.idiomatic: He was filial and fraternal by nature and steadfast in friendship and moral obligation.

sentences.zh: 閱經史，日有程限，至老不輟。

translations.literal: He read the classics and histories with a daily quota, and never stopped even in old age.
translations.idiomatic: He read the classics and histories according to a fixed daily schedule and never ceased, even in old age.

sentences.zh: 蕭用道，泰和人。

translations.literal: Xiao Yongdao was a native of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yongdao came from Taihe.

sentences.zh: 建文中，舉懷才抱德，詣闕試文章。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign he was recommended as one who cherished talent and embraced virtue, went to court, and was examined in composition.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwen reign he was recommended as a man of talent and virtue, went to court, and was tested in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 擢靖江王府長史，召入翰林，修《類要》。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Chief Secretary of the Prince of Jingjiang's establishment, summoned into the Hanlin Academy, and assigned to compile the 《Classified Essentials》.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Chief Secretary of the Prince of Jingjiang's household, summoned to the Hanlin Academy, and put to work compiling the 《Classified Essentials》.

sentences.zh: 燕師渡淮，與周是修同上書，指斥用事者。

translations.literal: When the Yan army crossed the Huai, he and Zhou Shixiu jointly submitted a memorial denouncing those in power.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army crossed the Huai River, he and Zhou Shixiu jointly submitted a memorial denouncing those then in power.

sentences.zh: 永樂時，預修《太祖實錄》，改右長史，從王之藩桂林。

translations.literal: During Yongle he took part in compiling the 《Veritable Records of Taizu》, was transferred to Right Chief Secretary, and followed the prince to his fief at Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongle he helped compile the 《Veritable Records of Taizu》, was made Right Chief Secretary, and accompanied the prince to his fief at Guilin.

sentences.zh: 嘗為王陳八事，曰：慎起居、寡嗜欲、勤學問、養德性、簡鞭撲之刑、無侵下人利、常接府僚以通群情、簡擇謹厚人以備差遣。

translations.literal: He once presented the prince with eight points, saying: be careful in daily routine; keep desires few; study diligently; cultivate moral nature; reduce flogging punishments; do not encroach on the interests of subordinates; regularly receive establishment officials to understand popular sentiment; and select careful, honest men to stand ready for assignments.
translations.idiomatic: He once set forth eight points for the prince: attend carefully to daily conduct; keep desires in check; pursue learning diligently; cultivate moral character; reduce corporal punishment; do not encroach on the interests of subordinates; regularly receive household officials to understand the mood of those below; and select careful, honest men for assignments.

sentences.zh: 又作《端禮》、《體仁》、《遵義》、《廣智》四門箴獻王。

translations.literal: He also composed admonitions for the four gates 《Correct Ritual》, 《Embodying Benevolence》, 《Following Righteousness》, and 《Broad Wisdom》 and presented them to the prince.
translations.idiomatic: He also composed admonitions for the four gates—the 《Correct Ritual》, 《Embodying Benevolence》, 《Following Righteousness》, and 《Broad Wisdom》 gates—and presented them to the prince.

sentences.zh: 久之，以疾乞歸。

translations.literal: After a long time he requested leave to return home on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he asked to retire home because of illness.

sentences.zh: 成祖怒，貶宣府鷂兒嶺巡檢，卒。

translations.literal: Emperor Chengzu was angry and demoted him to inspector at Ya'er Ridge in Xuanfu, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chengzu was enraged and demoted him to inspector at Ya'er Ridge in Xuanfu, where he died.

sentences.zh: 子亙，由進士官湖廣左布政使。

translations.literal: His son Gen, through the jinshi degree, rose to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gen, a jinshi, rose to serve as Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 天順四年，舉治行卓異，拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianshun he was recommended for outstanding governance and appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianshun he was commended for outstanding governance and appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 初，兩京尚書缺，多用布政使為之。

translations.literal: At first, when ministerial posts in the two capitals fell vacant, provincial administration commissioners were often appointed to them.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when ministerial posts in the two capitals fell vacant, provincial administration commissioners were often promoted to fill them.

sentences.zh: 自亙後，遂無拜尚書者。

translations.literal: After Gen, there were no longer appointments as minister.
translations.idiomatic: After Gen, no one in that path was again appointed minister.

sentences.zh: 亙重厚廉靜，而不善奏對。

translations.literal: Gen was grave, honest, and reserved, but not skilled at memorials and audience responses.
translations.idiomatic: Gen was grave, honest, and self-contained, but he was not adept at memorials and audience responses.

sentences.zh: 調南京，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Nanjing and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Nanjing, where he died.

sentences.zh: 宋訥，字仲敏，滑人。

translations.literal: Song Ne, style name Zhongmin, was a native of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Song Ne, whose style name was Zhongmin, came from Hua.

sentences.zh: 父壽卿，元侍御史。

translations.literal: His father Shouqing was an attendant censor of the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shouqing had been an attendant censor under the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 訥性持重，學問該博。

translations.literal: Ne by nature was steady and grave, and his learning was comprehensive.
translations.idiomatic: Ne was steady and grave by nature, and his learning was broad and thorough.

sentences.zh: 至正中，舉進士，任鹽山尹，棄官歸。

translations.literal: In the Zhizheng era he passed the jinshi examination, served as magistrate of Yanshan, and abandoned office to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhizheng era he passed the jinshi examination, served as magistrate of Yanshan, and then resigned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年，徵儒士十八人編《禮》、《樂》諸書，訥與焉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongwu eighteen Confucian scholars were summoned to compile the 《Rites》, 《Music》, and related books, and Ne was among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Hongwu eighteen Confucian scholars were summoned to compile the 《Rites》, 《Music》, and related works, and Ne was among them.

sentences.zh: 事竣，不仕歸。

translations.literal: When the work was finished he did not take office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished he declined further office and returned home.

sentences.zh: 久之，用四輔官杜斅薦，授國子助教。

translations.literal: After a long time, on the recommendation of Du Xiao, an official of the Four Chancellors, he was appointed Assistant Instructor at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, on the recommendation of Du Xiao, an official among the Four Chancellors, he was appointed Assistant Instructor at the National University.

sentences.zh: 以說經為學者所宗。

translations.literal: Because of his exposition of the classics he was regarded by scholars.
translations.idiomatic: His lectures on the classics made him a model among scholars.

sentences.zh: 十五年超遷翰林學士，命撰《宣聖廟碑》，稱旨，賞賚甚厚。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted out of turn to Hanlin Academician, ordered to compose the 《Stele for the Temple of the Sage Who Propagated the Teaching》, pleased the throne, and received very generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was promoted out of turn to Hanlin Academician, was ordered to compose the 《Stele for the Temple of the Sage Who Propagated the Teaching》, pleased the Emperor, and received very generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 改文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 嘗寒附火，燎脅下衣，至膚始覺。

translations.literal: Once in cold weather as he warmed himself by the fire, he scorched the garment under his arm and did not notice until it reached his skin.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while warming himself by the fire on a cold day, he scorched the garment under his arm and did not notice until it had reached his skin.

sentences.zh: 帝制文警之。

translations.literal: The Emperor composed a text to warn him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wrote an admonitory essay to warn him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷祭酒。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Chancellor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 時功臣子弟皆就學，及歲貢士嘗數千人。

translations.literal: At the time the sons and younger brothers of meritorious officials all came to study, and the annual tribute students sometimes numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the sons and younger brothers of meritorious officials all came to study, and the annual quota of tribute students sometimes reached several thousand.

sentences.zh: 訥為嚴立學規，終日端坐講解無虛晷，夜恒止學舍。

translations.literal: Ne strictly established school regulations, sat upright lecturing all day without idle moments, and always stayed in the dormitory at night.
translations.idiomatic: Ne established strict school regulations, sat upright lecturing throughout the day without a wasted hour, and always remained in the student dormitory at night.

sentences.zh: 十八年復開進士科，取士四百七十有奇，由太學者三之二。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the jinshi examination was reopened; more than four hundred and seventy men were selected, two-thirds of them from the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the jinshi examination was reopened; more than four hundred and seventy candidates were selected, two-thirds of them from the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 再策士，亦如之。

translations.literal: When policy questions were put to candidates again, it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace examination was held again, the result was much the same.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 制詞褒美。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript praised and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial rescript praised him in glowing terms.

sentences.zh: 助教金文徵等疾訥，構之吏部尚書余熂，牒令致仕。

translations.literal: Assistant Instructors Jin Wenzheng and others resented Ne, framed a case against him with Minister of Personnel Yu Bi, and sent a document ordering him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Instructors Jin Wenzheng and others resented Ne, plotted against him with Minister of Personnel Yu Bi, and issued a document ordering him to retire.

sentences.zh: 訥陛辭，帝驚問，大怒，誅熂、文徵等，留訥如故。

translations.literal: Ne took leave at court; the Emperor asked in alarm, grew greatly angry, executed Bi, Wenzheng, and the others, and kept Ne as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Ne came to take leave at court, the Emperor asked in alarm, flew into a rage, executed Bi, Wenzheng, and the others, and kept Ne in his post as before.

sentences.zh: 訥嘗病，帝曰：「訥有壽骨，無憂也。」

translations.literal: When Ne once fell ill, the Emperor said: "Ne has the bone structure of long life; there is no need to worry."
translations.idiomatic: When Ne once fell ill, the Emperor said, "Ne has the bone structure of long life; there is no need to worry."

sentences.zh: 尋愈。

translations.literal: Before long he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he recovered.

sentences.zh: 帝使畫工間訥，圖其像，危坐，有怒色。

translations.literal: The Emperor had a painter observe Ne secretly and paint his likeness: he sat upright with an angry expression.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had a painter observe Ne in secret and paint his likeness: Ne sat upright with an angry expression.

sentences.zh: 明日入對，帝問：「昨何怒？」

translations.literal: The next day when he entered for audience the Emperor asked: "Why were you angry yesterday?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when he came for audience, the Emperor asked, "Why were you angry yesterday?"

sentences.zh: 訥驚對曰：「諸生有趨踣者，碎茶器。

translations.literal: Ne answered in alarm: "Some students rushed and fell, breaking tea vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Ne answered in alarm, "Some students rushed and fell, breaking tea vessels.

sentences.zh: 臣愧失教，故自訟耳。

translations.literal: Your servant is ashamed at failing in instruction and therefore reproached himself.
translations.idiomatic: I am ashamed at having failed in instruction and was reproaching myself.

sentences.zh: 且陛下何自知之？」

translations.literal: Moreover, how did Your Majesty know this yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, how did Your Majesty know this?"

sentences.zh: 帝出圖。

translations.literal: The Emperor produced the painting.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor produced the painting.

sentences.zh: 訥頓首謝。

translations.literal: Ne bowed his head to the ground in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Ne kowtowed in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 長子麟，舉進士，擢御史，出為望江主簿。

translations.literal: His eldest son Lin passed the jinshi examination, was promoted to censor, and went out to serve as registrar of Wangjiang.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Lin passed the jinshi examination, was promoted to censor, and was sent out to serve as registrar of Wangjiang.

sentences.zh: 帝念訥老，召還侍。

translations.literal: The Emperor, mindful that Ne was old, summoned Lin back to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful that Ne was old, the Emperor summoned Lin back to attend his father.

sentences.zh: 二十三年春，訥病甚，乃止學舍。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-third year Ne was gravely ill and only then stopped staying in the dormitory.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-third year Ne fell gravely ill and only then stopped remaining in the student dormitory.

sentences.zh: 麟請歸私第，叱曰：「時當丁祭，敢不敬耶！」

translations.literal: Lin asked to return to the private residence, and he rebuked him, saying: "It is time for the ding sacrifice; how dare you be disrespectful!"
translations.idiomatic: When Lin asked to take him back to their private residence, he rebuked him, saying, "It is time for the ding sacrifice; how dare you be disrespectful!"

sentences.zh: 祭畢，舁歸舍而卒，年八十。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice was finished he was carried back to the dormitory and died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: When the sacrifice was finished he was carried back to the dormitory and died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 帝悼惜，自為文祭之。

translations.literal: The Emperor mourned and regretted his loss, and personally composed a text to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor mourned his loss and personally composed a funeral elegy to sacrifice to him.

sentences.zh: 又遣官祭於家，為治葬地。

translations.literal: He also sent officials to sacrifice at his home and arranged a burial site for him.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent officials to offer sacrifices at his home and provided a burial site.

sentences.zh: 文臣四品給祭葬者，自訥始。

translations.literal: The granting of sacrificial and burial honors to civil officials of the fourth rank began with Ne.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of granting sacrificial and burial honors to civil officials of the fourth rank began with Ne.

sentences.zh: 正德中。

translations.literal: During Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 謚文恪。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Wenge.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Wenge.

sentences.zh: 訥嘗應詔陳邊事，言：「海內乂安，惟沙漠尚煩聖慮。

translations.literal: Ne once responded to an imperial edict and set forth border affairs, saying: "Within the seas all is at peace; only the desert still troubles the sage mind.
translations.idiomatic: Ne once responded to an imperial edict on border affairs, saying, "Within the seas all is at peace; only the desert still weighs on the Emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 若窮追遠擊，未免勞費。

translations.literal: If one pursues to the limit and strikes far away, labor and expense cannot be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: If one pursues the enemy relentlessly and strikes deep into the distance, labor and expense cannot be avoided.

sentences.zh: 陛下為聖子神孫計，不過謹邊備而已。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, planning for sage sons and divine grandsons, need do no more than be careful in border defense.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, planning for the sake of future sage sons and divine grandsons, need do no more than maintain careful border defenses.

sentences.zh: 備邊在乎實兵，實兵在乎屯田。

translations.literal: Border defense lies in making troops real; making troops real lies in garrison farming.
translations.idiomatic: Border defense depends on maintaining effective forces, and effective forces depend on garrison farming.

sentences.zh: 漢趙充國將四萬騎，分屯緣邊九郡，而單於引卻。

translations.literal: In Han, Zhao Chongguo led forty thousand horsemen and divided them to garrison the nine border commanderies, and the Chanyu withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times Zhao Chongguo led forty thousand horsemen and distributed them in garrisons along the nine border commanderies, and the Chanyu withdrew.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜於諸將中選謀勇數人，以東西五百里為制，立法分屯，布列要害，遠近相應。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should select several men of strategy and courage from among the generals, take five hundred li east and west as the standard, establish law for divided garrison, deploy them at strategic points, and have distant and near positions respond to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should select several capable and courageous generals, take five hundred li east and west as the standard, establish regulations for distributed garrisons, deploy them at strategic points, and arrange for distant and nearby posts to support one another.

sentences.zh: 遇敵則戰，寇去則耕。

translations.literal: When encountering the enemy they fight; when raiders depart they farm.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy appears they fight; when raiders withdraw they farm.

sentences.zh: 此長策也。」

translations.literal: This is the long-term strategy."
translations.idiomatic: This is the sound long-term strategy."

sentences.zh: 帝頗采用其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor largely adopted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor largely adopted his advice.

sentences.zh: 訥既卒，帝思之。

translations.literal: After Ne died the Emperor thought of him.
translations.idiomatic: After Ne died the Emperor missed him.

sentences.zh: 官其次子復祖為司業，誡諸生守訥學規，違者罪至死。

translations.literal: He appointed Ne's second son Fuzu as Vice Chancellor and admonished the students to keep Ne's school regulations; violators were punished up to death.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Ne's second son Fuzu as Vice Chancellor and admonished the students to observe Ne's school regulations; violators were punished even with death.

sentences.zh: 明開國時即重師儒官。

translations.literal: At the founding of Ming, posts for masters and Confucian scholars were already highly valued.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding of the dynasty, Ming already placed great weight on posts for teachers and Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 許存仁、魏觀為祭酒，老成端謹；

translations.literal: Xu Cunren and Wei Guan served as Chancellor; they were mature, steady, and careful;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Cunren and Wei Guan served as Chancellor; they were mature, steady, and dignified;

sentences.zh: 訥稍晚進，最蒙遇。

translations.literal: Ne entered somewhat later and received the greatest favor.
translations.idiomatic: Ne entered somewhat later and enjoyed the greatest imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 與訥定學規者，司業王嘉會、龔斅。

translations.literal: Those who with Ne established the school regulations were Vice Chancellors Wang Jiahui and Gong Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Those who worked with Ne to establish the school regulations were Vice Chancellors Wang Jiahui and Gong Xiao.

sentences.zh: 三人年俱高，須發皓白，終日危坐，堂上肅然。

translations.literal: All three were advanced in years, their beards and hair snow-white; they sat upright all day, and the hall was solemn.
translations.idiomatic: All three were advanced in years, with snow-white beards and hair; they sat upright throughout the day, and the hall was solemn.

sentences.zh: 而張美和、聶鉉、貝瓊等皆名儒，當洪武時，先後為博士、助教、學錄，以故諸生多所成就。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhang Meihe, Nie Xuan, Bei Qiong, and others were all famous Confucians; during Hongwu they served in succession as Erudite, Assistant Instructor, and Recorder, and for this reason many students achieved distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Meihe, Nie Xuan, Bei Qiong, and others were all renowned Confucian scholars; during Hongwu they served in turn as Erudite, Assistant Instructor, and Recorder, and for this reason many students achieved distinction.

sentences.zh: 魏觀事別載。

translations.literal: Wei Guan's affairs are recorded separately.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan's biography is recorded separately.

sentences.zh: 嘉會，字原禮，嘉興人。

translations.literal: Jiahui, style name Yuanli, was a native of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Jiahui, whose style name was Yuanli, came from Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 以薦征，累官國子監司業。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was summoned and rose through posts to Vice Chancellor of the Directorate of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned on recommendation, he rose through the ranks to Vice Chancellor of the Directorate of the National University.

sentences.zh: 十六年，亦以老請歸，優詔留之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he too requested leave to return home on grounds of age, and a gracious edict kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he too asked to retire on grounds of age, and a gracious edict kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 年八十卒，賻恤甚厚。

translations.literal: He died at eighty, and funeral gifts and condolence payments were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty, and the funeral gifts and condolence payments were very generous.

sentences.zh: 許存仁。

translations.literal: Xu Cunren.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Cunren.

sentences.zh: 名元，以字行，金華許謙子也。

translations.literal: His personal name was Yuan; he was known by his style name; he was the son of Xu Qian of Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: His personal name was Yuan, but he was known by his style name; he was the son of Xu Qian of Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 太祖素聞謙名，克金華，訪得存仁。

translations.literal: Taizu had long heard of Qian's reputation; when he took Jinhua he sought out and found Cunren.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had long heard of Qian's reputation; when he captured Jinhua he sought out Cunren and found him.

sentences.zh: 與語大悅，命傅諸子。

translations.literal: After speaking with him he was greatly pleased and ordered him to instruct the princes.
translations.idiomatic: After speaking with him he was greatly pleased and ordered him to instruct the imperial sons.

sentences.zh: 擢國子博士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Erudite at the Directorate of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Erudite at the Directorate of the National University.

sentences.zh: 嘗命講《尚書·洪範》休咎征之說。

translations.literal: He was once ordered to lecture on the doctrine of blessings, calamities, and portents in the 《Hongfan》 chapter of the 《Book of Documents》.
translations.idiomatic: He was once ordered to expound the doctrine of blessings, calamities, and portents in the 《Hongfan》 chapter of the 《Book of Documents》.

sentences.zh: 又嘗問《孟子》何說為要。

translations.literal: He was also once asked which teaching in the 《Mencius》 was most important.
translations.idiomatic: He was also once asked which teaching in the 《Mencius》 was most essential.

sentences.zh: 存仁以行王道、省刑、薄賦對。

translations.literal: Cunren answered with practicing the kingly way, reducing punishments, and lightening taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Cunren answered that the essentials were practicing the kingly way, reducing punishments, and lightening taxes.

sentences.zh: 吳元年擢祭酒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wu he was promoted to Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Wu reign he was promoted to Chancellor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 存仁出入左右垂十年，自稽古禮文事，至進退人才，無不與論議。

translations.literal: Cunren attended at left and right for nearly ten years; from investigating ancient rites and literary matters, to advancing and dismissing talent, there was nothing he did not discuss and deliberate on.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly ten years Cunren attended the prince at his side. Whether the topic was ancient rites and ceremonial texts or the promotion and dismissal of men of talent, there was nothing on which he was not consulted.

sentences.zh: 既將議即大位，而存仁告歸。

translations.literal: When they were about to discuss assuming the supreme position, Cunren requested to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Just as they were about to discuss his accession to the throne, Cunren asked to retire and go home.

sentences.zh: 司業劉丞直曰：「主上方應天順人，公宜稍待。」

translations.literal: Vice Chancellor Liu Chengzhi said: "The lord is about to respond to Heaven and accord with the people; you, sir, ought to wait a little longer.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Chancellor Liu Chengzhi said, "Our lord is about to respond to Heaven and win the people's assent; you, sir, ought to wait a little longer.

sentences.zh: 存仁不聽，果忤旨。

translations.literal: Cunren would not listen, and indeed offended the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: Cunren refused to listen, and in the end ran afoul of the imperial will.

sentences.zh: 僉事程孔昭劾其隱事，遂逮死獄中。

translations.literal: Secretariat Officer Cheng Kongzhao impeached him for hidden matters, and he was arrested and died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Officer Cheng Kongzhao impeached him on charges of concealed misconduct, and he was arrested and died in prison.

sentences.zh: 張美和，名九韶，以字行，清江人。

translations.literal: Zhang Meihe, personal name Jiushao, known by his style name, was a native of Qingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Meihe, whose personal name was Jiushao but who was known by his style name, was a native of Qingjiang.

sentences.zh: 能詞賦。

translations.literal: He was skilled at lyric poetry and rhapsodies.
translations.idiomatic: He was accomplished in lyric poetry and rhapsodic prose.

sentences.zh: 元末，累舉不仕。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan, he was repeatedly recommended but refused office.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan dynasty he was repeatedly recommended for office but declined each time.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，以薦為縣學教諭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu, on recommendation he was appointed Instructor at the county school.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongwu, on recommendation he was appointed instructor at the county school.

sentences.zh: 後遷國子助教，改翰林院編修。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Assistant Instructor at the National University, then changed to Compiler in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to assistant instructor at the National University and then appointed compiler in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 致仕歸，帝親為文賜之。

translations.literal: He retired and returned home, and the Emperor personally wrote an essay to bestow upon him.
translations.idiomatic: When he retired and returned home, the Emperor personally composed an essay and bestowed it upon him.

sentences.zh: 復與錢宰等並征，修《書》傳，既成，遣還。

translations.literal: He was again summoned together with Qian Zai and others to compile the commentary on the 《Book of Documents》; when it was finished, they were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned again together with Qian Zai and others to compile the commentary on the 《Book of Documents》; when the work was finished, they were sent home.

sentences.zh: 聶鉉，字器之，美和同邑人。

translations.literal: Nie Xuan, style name Qizhi, was a fellow townsman of Meihe.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Xuan, style name Qizhi, was from the same district as Meihe.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 為廣宗丞，疏免旱災稅。

translations.literal: As Assistant Magistrate of Guangzong, he memorialized to remit drought-disaster taxes.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as assistant magistrate of Guangzong, he memorialized the throne to remit taxes owed because of drought.

sentences.zh: 秩滿入覲，獻《南都賦》及《洪武聖德詩》。

translations.literal: When his term expired he came to audience and presented the 《Fu on the Southern Capital》 and the 《Poem on Hongwu's Sagely Virtue》.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he came to court and presented the 《Fu on the Southern Capital》 and the 《Poem on Hongwu's Sagely Virtue》.

sentences.zh: 授翰林院待制，改國子助教，遷典籍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin Academy Attendant Draftsman, changed to Assistant Instructor at the National University, and promoted to Archivist.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed attendant draftsman in the Hanlin Academy, then transferred to assistant instructor at the National University, and later promoted to archivist.

sentences.zh: 與美和同賜歸。

translations.literal: He was granted leave to return home together with Meihe.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted leave to return home together with Meihe.

sentences.zh: 十八年復召典會試，欲留用之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was again summoned to preside over the metropolitan examination; the court wished to keep and employ him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was summoned again to preside over the metropolitan examination, and the court wished to retain him in office.

sentences.zh: 乞便地自養。

translations.literal: He begged to retire to a convenient place to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire to a convenient place where he could live on his own.

sentences.zh: 令食廬陵教諭俸，終其身。

translations.literal: He was ordered to receive the salary of Instructor of Luling for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the salary of an instructor in Luling for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 貝瓊，字廷琚，崇德人。

translations.literal: Bei Qiong, style name Tingju, was a native of Chongde.
translations.idiomatic: Bei Qiong, style name Tingju, was a native of Chongde.

sentences.zh: 性坦率，篤誌好學，年四十八，始領鄉薦。

translations.literal: Frank by nature and devoted to learning, he was forty-eight before he first received the provincial recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Frank by nature and deeply committed to study, he was forty-eight before he first received a provincial recommendation.

sentences.zh: 張士誠屢辟不就。

translations.literal: Zhang Shicheng repeatedly invited him but he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng repeatedly invited him into service, but he always refused.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，聘修《元史》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu, he was engaged to compile the 《History of the Yuan》.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Hongwu reign he was engaged to help compile the 《History of the Yuan》.

sentences.zh: 既成，受賜歸。

translations.literal: When it was finished, he received rewards and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, he received imperial rewards and returned home.

sentences.zh: 六年以儒士舉，除國子助教。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, recommended as a Confucian scholar, he was appointed Assistant Instructor at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, recommended as a Confucian scholar, he was appointed assistant instructor at the National University.

sentences.zh: 瓊嘗慨古樂不作，為《大韶賦》以見誌。

translations.literal: Qiong once lamented that ancient music was no longer performed and wrote the 《Great Shao Rhapsody》 to express his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong once lamented that the music of antiquity was no longer performed and wrote the 《Great Shao Rhapsody》 to declare his convictions.

sentences.zh: 宋濂之為司業也，建議立四學，並祀舜、禹、湯、文為先聖。

translations.literal: When Song Lian served as Vice Chancellor, he proposed establishing four schools and jointly enshrining Shun, Yu, Tang, and King Wen as primordial sages.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Lian served as vice chancellor, he proposed establishing four schools and jointly enshrining Shun, Yu, Tang, and King Wen as primordial sages.

sentences.zh: 太祖既絀其說，瓊復為《釋奠解》駁之，識者多是瓊議。

translations.literal: After Taizu had rejected his proposal, Qiong wrote the 《Explanation of the Sacrifice Offering》 to refute it, and informed opinion largely sided with Qiong's view.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu had rejected Song's proposal, Qiong wrote the 《Explanation of the Sacrifice Offering》 to rebut it, and informed opinion largely sided with Qiong.

sentences.zh: 與美和、鉉齊名，時稱「成均三助」。

translations.literal: He was equally famed with Meihe and Xuan, and at the time they were called "the Three Assistant Instructors of the Imperial Academy."
translations.idiomatic: He was as renowned as Meihe and Xuan, and at the time they were known as "the Three Assistant Instructors of the Imperial Academy."

sentences.zh: 九年改官中都國子監，教勛臣子弟。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to the Metropolitan Directorate of the National University at Zhongdu to instruct the sons of meritorious officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was transferred to the metropolitan directorate of the National University at Zhongdu to instruct the sons of meritorious officials.

sentences.zh: 瓊學行素優，將校武臣皆知禮重。

translations.literal: Qiong's learning and conduct had always been excellent, and military officers and commanders all knew to honor ritual and show respect.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong's learning and conduct had long been outstanding, and even military officers and commanders learned to honor ritual and treat him with respect.

sentences.zh: 十一年致仕，卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he retired from office and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he retired from office and died.

sentences.zh: 趙俶，字本初，山陰人。

translations.literal: Zhao Chu, style name Benchu, was a native of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chu, style name Benchu, was a native of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 元進士。

translations.literal: A Yuan-dynasty jinshi graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a jinshi graduate of the Yuan dynasty.

sentences.zh: 洪武六年，征授國子博士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongwu, he was summoned and appointed Erudite at the Directorate of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Hongwu he was summoned and appointed erudite at the Directorate of the National University.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗禦奉天殿，召俶及錢宰、貝瓊等曰：「汝等一以孔子所定經書為教，慎勿雜蘇秦、張儀縱橫之言。」

translations.literal: The Emperor once held court in the Hall of Upholding Heaven, summoned Chu along with Qian Zai, Bei Qiong, and others, and said: "You shall take exclusively the classics established by Confucius as your teaching; be careful not to mix in the stratagem rhetoric of Su Qin and Zhang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once held court in the Hall of Upholding Heaven and summoned Chu, Qian Zai, Bei Qiong, and others, saying, "You must teach only the classics established by Confucius as your teaching. Be careful not to introduce the stratagem rhetoric of Su Qin and Zhang Yi.

sentences.zh: 諸臣頓首受命。

translations.literal: The officials all kowtowed and accepted the command.
translations.idiomatic: The officials all kowtowed and accepted the command.

sentences.zh: 俶因請頒正定《十三經》於天下，屏《戰國策》及陰陽讖卜諸書，勿列學宮。

translations.literal: Chu thereupon requested that the corrected 《Thirteen Classics》 be promulgated throughout the realm, and that the 《Strategies of the Warring States》 together with books on yin-yang lore, prophecy, and divination be excluded and not placed in the academies.
translations.idiomatic: Chu then asked that the corrected 《Thirteen Classics》 be promulgated throughout the realm, and that the 《Strategies of the Warring States》 together with works on yin-yang lore, prophecy, and divination be barred from the academies.

sentences.zh: 明年擇諸生穎異者三十五人，命俶專領之，教以古文。

translations.literal: The next year thirty-five outstanding students were selected, and Chu was ordered to take charge of them exclusively and teach them ancient-style prose.
translations.idiomatic: The following year thirty-five exceptionally gifted students were chosen, and Chu was ordered to take charge of them and teach them ancient-style prose.

sentences.zh: 尋擢李擴、黃義等入文華、武英二堂說書，皆見用。

translations.literal: Soon Li Kuo, Huang Yi, and others were promoted to lecture in the Wenhua and Wuying halls, and all were employed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Kuo, Huang Yi, and others were promoted to lecture in the Wenhua and Wuying halls, and all were put to use.

sentences.zh: 九年，御史臺言：「博士俶以《詩經》教成均四年，其弟子多為方嶽重臣及持節各部者。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Censorate reported: "Erudite Chu has taught the 《Classic of Poetry》 at the Imperial Academy for four years; many of his disciples have become great ministers of provincial governors and envoys holding imperial insignia in various departments.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Censorate reported, "Erudite Chu has taught the 《Classic of Poetry》 at the Imperial Academy for four years, and many of his disciples have become leading provincial ministers and imperial envoys in various departments.

sentences.zh: 今年逾懸車，請賜骸骨。」

translations.literal: This year he has passed the age for retiring, and requests to be granted leave to return his bones.
translations.idiomatic: This year he has passed the age of retirement and asks to be permitted to return home.

sentences.zh: 於是以翰林院待制致仕，賜內帑錢治裝。

translations.literal: Thereupon he retired with the title Hanlin Academy Attendant Draftsman and was granted money from the inner treasury for travel expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he retired with the title of Hanlin attendant draftsman and was granted money from the inner treasury for his journey home.

sentences.zh: 宋濂率同官暨諸生千余人送之。

translations.literal: Song Lian led more than a thousand fellow officials and students to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: Song Lian led more than a thousand fellow officials and students to see him off.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 子圭玉，兵部侍郎，出知萊州，有聲。

translations.literal: His son Guiyu became Vice Minister of War and went out to serve as Prefect of Laizhou, where he won renown.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guiyu became vice minister of war and went out to serve as prefect of Laizhou, where he earned a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 錢宰，字子予，會稽人。

translations.literal: Qian Zai, style name Ziyu, was a native of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Zai, style name Ziyu, was a native of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 吳越武肅王十四世孫。

translations.literal: He was a fourteenth-generation descendant of Wuyue's King Wusu.
translations.idiomatic: He was a fourteenth-generation descendant of Wuyue's King Wusu.

sentences.zh: 至正間中甲科，親老不仕。

translations.literal: During the Zhizheng era he passed the highest grade of the examination, but because his parents were aged he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhizheng era he passed the highest grade of the civil examination, but because his parents were elderly he declined office.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年，征為國子助教。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongwu he was summoned as Assistant Instructor at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Hongwu he was summoned to serve as assistant instructor at the National University.

sentences.zh: 作《金陵形勝論》、《歷代帝王樂章》，皆稱旨。

translations.literal: He wrote the 《Treatise on Jinling's Strategic Terrain》 and the 《Music Hymns of Emperors Through the Ages》, all of which pleased the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the 《Treatise on Jinling's Strategic Terrain》 and the 《Music Hymns of Emperors Through the Ages》, both of which pleased the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 十年乞休。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 進博士，賜敕遣歸。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Erudite, granted an imperial edict, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to erudite, granted an imperial edict, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 至二十七年，帝觀蔡氏《書傳》，象緯運行，與朱子《詩傳》相悖，其他註與鄱陽鄒季友所論有未安者。

translations.literal: By the twenty-seventh year, when the Emperor examined the Cai family's 《Commentary on the Book of Documents》, its account of celestial movements conflicted with Zhu Xi's 《Commentary on the Classic of Poetry》, and other annotations also contained points that disagreed with Zou Jiyou of Poyang's arguments in unsatisfactory ways.
translations.idiomatic: By the twenty-seventh year, when the Emperor reviewed the Cai family's 《Commentary on the Book of Documents》, its account of the movements of the heavens and constellations conflicted with Zhu Xi's 《Commentary on the Classic of Poetry》, and other notes also contained points that Zou Jiyou of Poyang had shown to be unsatisfactory.

sentences.zh: 征天下宿儒訂正之。

translations.literal: Established scholars throughout the realm were summoned to revise it.
translations.idiomatic: Established scholars throughout the realm were summoned to revise the work.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書唐鐸舉宰及致仕編修張美和、助教靳權等。

translations.literal: Minister of War Tang Duo recommended Zai along with retired Compiler Zhang Meihe, Assistant Instructor Jin Quan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Tang Duo recommended Zai together with the retired compiler Zhang Meihe, assistant instructor Jin Quan, and others.

sentences.zh: 行人馳傳征至，命劉三吾總其事。

translations.literal: Court envoys were dispatched by relay post to summon them, and Liu Sanwu was ordered to oversee the work.
translations.idiomatic: Court envoys were sent by relay post to summon them, and Liu Sanwu was ordered to direct the project.

sentences.zh: 江東諸門酒樓成，賜百官鈔，宴其上。

translations.literal: When the wine towers at the several gates east of the river were completed, paper money was bestowed on the officials and a banquet was held atop them.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine towers at the several gates east of the river were completed, the officials were granted paper money and feasted on their upper floors.

sentences.zh: 宰等賦詩謝。

translations.literal: Zai and the others composed poems in gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Zai and the others composed poems in thanks.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 諭諸儒年老願歸者，先遣之。

translations.literal: He instructed that among the scholars, those advanced in age who wished to return home should be sent away first.
translations.idiomatic: He announced that any of the scholars who were old and wished to go home should be sent away first.

sentences.zh: 宰年最高，請留。

translations.literal: Zai was the eldest and asked to remain.
translations.idiomatic: Zai was the oldest among them and asked to stay.

sentences.zh: 帝喜。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 書成，賜名《書傳會選》，頒行天下。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, it was given the title 《Collected Selections of Commentaries on the Book of Documents》 and promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, it was given the title 《Collected Selections of Commentaries on the Book of Documents》 and issued throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 厚賜，令馳驛歸。

translations.literal: He was richly rewarded and ordered to return home by express relay.
translations.idiomatic: He received generous rewards and was ordered to return home by express relay.

sentences.zh: 卒年九十六。

translations.literal: He died at the age of ninety-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of ninety-six.

sentences.zh: 又蕭執者，字子所，泰和人。

translations.literal: There was also Xiao Zhi, style name Zisuo, a native of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Xiao Zhi, style name Zisuo, a native of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年鄉舉，為國子學錄。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu he passed the provincial examination and became Recorder at the Directorate of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Hongwu he passed the provincial examination and was appointed recorder at the Directorate of the National University.

sentences.zh: 明年夏至，帝有事北郊，召尚書吳琳、主事宋濂率文學士以從。

translations.literal: The next year, at the summer solstice, when the Emperor performed rites at the Northern Suburb, he summoned Minister Wu Lin and Principal Secretary Song Lian to lead literary scholars to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, at the summer solstice, when the Emperor performed rites at the Northern Suburb, he summoned Minister Wu Lin and principal secretary Song Lian to lead literary scholars in attendance.

sentences.zh: 執偕陶凱等十二人入見齋所。

translations.literal: Zhi entered the fasting quarters together with Tao Kai and eleven others to be received in audience.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi entered the fasting quarters together with Tao Kai and eleven others to be received in audience.

sentences.zh: 令賦詩，復令賦山梔花。

translations.literal: They were ordered to compose poems, and then ordered again to compose on gardenia blossoms.
translations.idiomatic: They were ordered to compose poems, and then ordered again to compose on gardenia blossoms.

sentences.zh: 獨喜執作，遍示諸臣，寵眷傾一時。

translations.literal: The Emperor alone favored Zhi's compositions, showed them to all the ministers, and his special favor at that moment knew no equal.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor alone favored Zhi's compositions, showed them to all the ministers, and for a time his favor toward Zhi surpassed all others.

sentences.zh: 時帝留意文學，往往親試廷臣，執與陳觀知遇尤異。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor paid close attention to literature and often personally tested court officials himself; Zhi and Chen Guan enjoyed especially remarkable imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Emperor took a keen interest in literature and often tested court officials himself; Zhi and Chen Guan enjoyed especially remarkable favor.

sentences.zh: 觀以訓導入覲，試《王猛捫CB論》，立擢陜西參政。

translations.literal: Guan entered the capital as an instructor to audience; tested on the 《Essay on Wang Meng Picking Lice》, he was immediately promoted to Administrative Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan came to court in his capacity as an instructor, he was tested on the 《Essay on Wang Meng Picking Lice》 and was immediately promoted to administrative commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 尋召還侍左右。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled to attend at the Emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled to attend at the Emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 應制作《鐘山賦》，賜金幣。

translations.literal: When summoned to compose at imperial command, he wrote the 《Zhong Mountain Rhapsody》 and was granted gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned to compose at imperial command, he wrote the 《Zhong Mountain Rhapsody》 and was granted gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 在陜以廉謹稱。

translations.literal: While in Shaanxi he was known for integrity and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in Shaanxi he was known for integrity and prudence.

sentences.zh: 或問陜產金何狀。

translations.literal: Someone asked what the gold produced in Shaanxi looked like.
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked what the gold produced in Shaanxi looked like.

sentences.zh: 觀大驚曰：「吾備位藩寮，何金之問！」

translations.literal: Guan was greatly alarmed and said: "I merely hold a nominal post among the provincial officials—what business have I with questions about gold!
translations.idiomatic: Guan was greatly alarmed and said, "I merely hold a nominal post among the provincial officials—why ask me about gold!

sentences.zh: 其卒也，妻子幾無以自存。

translations.literal: When he died, his wife and children could barely support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his wife and children could barely support themselves.

sentences.zh: 而執以親老乞歸，親沒廬墓側。

translations.literal: Zhi, for his part, begged to return home because his parents were aged; when they died he built a hut beside their graves.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, for his part, asked to return home because his parents were elderly; when they died he built a hut beside their graves and mourned there.

sentences.zh: 申國公鄧鎮剿龍泉寇，不戢下。

translations.literal: Duke of Shen Deng Zhen was suppressing bandits at Longquan and could not restrain his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Shen Deng Zhen was suppressing bandits at Longquan and could not restrain his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 執往責之，鎮為禁止，邑人以安。

translations.literal: Zhi went to rebuke him; Zhen thereupon forbade the misconduct, and the people of the district were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi went to rebuke him; Zhen then put a stop to the abuses, and the people of the district were at peace.

sentences.zh: 兩人皆篤行君子也。

translations.literal: Both men were men of sincere conduct and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were men of sincere conduct and integrity.

sentences.zh: 李叔正，字克正，初名宗頤，靖安人。

translations.literal: Li Shuzheng, style name Kezheng, originally named Zongyi, was a native of Jing'an.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shuzheng, style name Kezheng, originally named Zongyi, was a native of Jing'an.

sentences.zh: 年十二能詩，長益淹博。

translations.literal: At twelve he could compose poetry; as he grew older he became ever more broadly learned.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he could already compose poetry, and as he grew older he became ever more broadly learned.

sentences.zh: 時江西有十才子，叔正其一也。

translations.literal: At the time Jiangxi had ten literary talents, and Shuzheng was one of them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jiangxi had ten celebrated literary talents, and Shuzheng was one of them.

sentences.zh: 以薦授國子學正。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was appointed Rectifier of Studies at the Directorate of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he was appointed rectifier of studies at the Directorate of the National University.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，告歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu he requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Hongwu reign he asked to retire and return home.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復以薦為學正，遷渭南丞。

translations.literal: Before long, on recommendation again he became Rectifier of Studies and was transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, recommended again, he became rectifier of studies and was transferred to assistant magistrate of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 同州蒲城人爭地界，累年不決。

translations.literal: People of Pucheng in Tongzhou disputed a land boundary for many years without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Pucheng in Tongzhou disputed a land boundary for many years without resolution.

sentences.zh: 行省以委叔正，單騎至，剖數語立決。

translations.literal: The provincial administration entrusted the matter to Shuzheng; he arrived alone on horseback and settled it at once with a few clarifying words.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial administration entrusted the matter to Shuzheng; he rode there alone and settled it at once with a few clarifying words.

sentences.zh: 渭南歲輸糧二萬，豪右與猾吏為奸，田無定額，叔正履畝丈量。

translations.literal: Weinan had to deliver twenty thousand piculs of grain annually; powerful families and corrupt clerks colluded in fraud, and fields had no fixed quotas, so Shuzheng measured every mu on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Weinan had to deliver twenty thousand piculs of grain each year; powerful families and corrupt clerks colluded in fraud, and fields had no fixed quotas, so Shuzheng went out and measured every mu himself.

sentences.zh: 立法精密，諸弊盡剔。

translations.literal: The regulations he established were precise and thorough, and every abuse was eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: The regulations he established were precise and thorough, and every abuse was eliminated.

sentences.zh: 遷興化知縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Magistrate of Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 尋召為禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned to serve as vice director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 以年老乞歸，不許，改國子助教。

translations.literal: He begged to return home on grounds of age but was refused and was changed to Assistant Instructor at the National University instead.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire on grounds of age, but the request was denied and he was reassigned as assistant instructor at the National University instead.

sentences.zh: 於是叔正三至太學矣。

translations.literal: Thus Shuzheng came to the Imperial Academy for the third time.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Shuzheng came to the Imperial Academy for the third time.

sentences.zh: 帝方銳意文治，於國學人材尤加意。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then keenly devoted to civil governance, and paid especial attention to talent at the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was then keenly devoted to civil governance and took especial care with talent at the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 然諸生多貴胄，不率教。

translations.literal: Yet most of the students were from noble families and did not follow the teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Yet most of the students were sons of the nobility and refused to obey the rules of instruction.

sentences.zh: 叔正嚴立規條，旦夕端坐，督課無倦色。

translations.literal: Shuzheng strictly established regulations, sat upright morning and evening, and supervised lessons without a trace of weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzheng established strict regulations, sat upright from morning till evening, and supervised lessons without ever showing weariness.

sentences.zh: 朝論賢之。

translations.literal: Court opinion held him worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Official opinion at court praised him as worthy.

sentences.zh: 擢監察御史，奉命巡嶺表。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Supervising Censor and ordered on imperial command to inspect the regions beyond the Ling mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising censor and ordered to inspect the Lingnan region.

sentences.zh: 瓊州府吏訐其守踞公座簽表文，叔正鞫之，守得白，抵吏罪。

translations.literal: A clerk in Qiongzhou Prefecture accused the prefect of occupying the official seat to sign a memorial; Shuzheng examined the case, the prefect was cleared, and the clerk was held guilty.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk in Qiongzhou Prefecture accused the prefect of improperly occupying the official seat to sign a memorial. Shuzheng investigated the case, cleared the prefect, and punished the clerk.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之曰：「人言老御史懦，乃明斷如是耶。」

translations.literal: Taizu praised him and said, "People say the old censor is timid — yet he is this clear and decisive!
translations.idiomatic: Taizu praised him, saying, "People say the old censor is timid — yet see how clear and decisive he is!

sentences.zh: 累官禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 十四年進尚書，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to Minister and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to minister and died in office.

sentences.zh: 叔正妻夏氏，陳友諒陷南昌時，投井死。

translations.literal: Shuzheng's wife, Lady Xia, when Chen Youliang took Nanchang, threw herself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzheng's wife, Lady Xia, threw herself into a well and died when Chen Youliang captured Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 叔正感其義，終身不復娶。

translations.literal: Moved by her righteousness, Shuzheng never married again in his lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by her fidelity, Shuzheng never remarried for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 劉崧，字子高，泰和人，舊名楚。

translations.literal: Liu Song, style name Zigao, was a native of Taihe; his former name was Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song, style name Zigao, was a native of Taihe; he had formerly been named Chu.

sentences.zh: 家貧力學，寒無壚火，手皸裂而鈔錄不輟。

translations.literal: His family was poor but he studied diligently; in the cold he had no brazier fire, and though his hands cracked with chapped skin he never stopped copying and transcribing.
translations.idiomatic: Though his family was poor, he studied tirelessly; in winter he had no brazier to warm himself, and even when his hands cracked with chapped skin he never stopped copying texts.

sentences.zh: 元末舉於鄉。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan dynasty he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年舉經明行修，改今名。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was selected for "Classics Bright and Conduct Cultivated" and his name was changed to the present one.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongwu he was selected in the "Classics Bright and Conduct Cultivated" category, and his name was changed to the present one.

sentences.zh: 召見奉天殿，授兵部職方司郎中。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience in the Hall of Upholding Heaven, he was appointed Director in the Bureau of Appointments in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience in the Hall of Upholding Heaven, he was appointed director in the Bureau of Appointments in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 奉命征糧鎮江。

translations.literal: On orders he collected grain levies in Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial orders he went to collect grain levies in Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 鎮江多勛臣田，租賦為民累，崧力請得少減。

translations.literal: Zhenjiang had many fields belonging to meritorious officials, and rent and tax burdens weighed on the people; Song forcefully petitioned and obtained a partial reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Many fields in Zhenjiang belonged to meritorious officials, and rent and tax burdens weighed heavily on the people; Song pressed his petition and won a partial reduction.

sentences.zh: 遷北平按察司副使，輕刑省事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Beiping Surveillance Commission, where he lightened punishments and streamlined administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice commissioner of the Beiping Surveillance Commission, where he lightened punishments and streamlined administration.

sentences.zh: 招集流亡，民鹹復業。

translations.literal: He gathered the displaced and wandering, and the people all returned to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the displaced and wandering, and the people all returned to their fields and trades.

sentences.zh: 立文天祥祠於學宮之側。

translations.literal: He established a shrine to Wen Tianxiang beside the school.
translations.idiomatic: He established a shrine to Wen Tianxiang beside the school compound.

sentences.zh: 勒石學門，示府縣勿以徭役累諸生。

translations.literal: He had a stone inscribed at the school gate, instructing prefectures and counties not to burden students with corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: He had a stone inscribed at the school gate instructing prefectures and counties not to burden students with corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 嘗請減僻地驛馬，以益宛平。

translations.literal: He once requested reducing post horses in remote areas in order to increase those at Wanping.
translations.idiomatic: He once petitioned to reduce post horses in remote areas so that Wanping could be better supplied.

sentences.zh: 帝可其奏，顧謂侍臣曰：「驛傳勞逸不均久矣，崧能言之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his memorial and, turning to the attending ministers, said, "For so long the relay stations have been uneven in labor and ease — Song was able to speak to this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved his memorial and, turning to the attending ministers, said, "For so long the relay stations have been uneven in labor and ease — Song was able to put his finger on it.

sentences.zh: 牧民不當如是耶？」

translations.literal: Should not one who governs the people act thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Is this not how one who governs the people ought to act?"

sentences.zh: 為胡惟庸所惡，坐事謫輸作。

translations.literal: He was hated by Hu Weiyong and, convicted on a charge, was demoted to corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: He was hated by Hu Weiyong and, convicted on a charge, was demoted to corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 尋放歸。

translations.literal: Before long he was released and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 十三年，惟庸誅，征拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, after Weiyong was executed, he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, after Weiyong was executed, he was summoned and appointed vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 雷震謹身殿，帝廷諭群臣陳得失。

translations.literal: Lightning struck the Hall of Self-Cultivation, and at court the Emperor instructed the assembled ministers to set forth what was right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Lightning struck the Hall of Self-Cultivation, and at court the Emperor instructed the assembled ministers to speak frankly of what was right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 崧頓首，以修德行仁對。

translations.literal: Song prostrated himself and answered that one should cultivate virtue and practice benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Song prostrated himself and answered that the remedy lay in cultivating virtue and practicing benevolence.

sentences.zh: 尋致仕。

translations.literal: Before long he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，與前刑部尚書李敬並征。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year he was summoned together with the former Minister of Punishment, Li Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year he was summoned together with the former minister of punishment, Li Jing.

sentences.zh: 拜敬國子祭酒，而崧為司業。

translations.literal: Jing was appointed Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, while Song became Vice Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was appointed chancellor of the Directorate of Education, while Song became vice chancellor.

sentences.zh: 賜鞍馬，令朝夕見，見輒燕語移時。

translations.literal: They were granted saddles and horses and ordered to attend morning and evening; whenever they were received, the Emperor would converse with them at ease for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: They were granted saddles and horses and ordered to attend morning and evening; whenever they were received, the Emperor would converse with them informally for a long while.

sentences.zh: 未旬日卒。

translations.literal: In less than ten days he died.
translations.idiomatic: In less than ten days he died.

sentences.zh: 疾作，猶強坐訓諸生。

translations.literal: When illness came upon him, he still forced himself to sit upright and instruct the students.
translations.idiomatic: When illness struck, he still forced himself to sit upright and instruct the students.

sentences.zh: 及革，敬問所欲言。

translations.literal: When the illness turned critical, Jing asked what he wished to say.
translations.idiomatic: When the illness turned critical, Jing asked whether he had anything he wished to say.

sentences.zh: 曰：「天子遣崧教國子，將責以成功，而遽死乎！」

translations.literal: He said, "The Son of Heaven sent Song to instruct the imperial students and will hold him accountable for success — yet he dies so suddenly!"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The Son of Heaven sent Song to instruct the imperial students and will hold him accountable for success — yet he dies so suddenly!"

sentences.zh: 無一語及家事。

translations.literal: Not one word touched on family affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Not one word touched on family affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝命有司治殯殮，親為文祭之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the relevant offices to arrange the burial and personally composed a eulogy to offer sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the relevant offices to arrange the burial and personally composed a eulogy to offer sacrifice to him.

sentences.zh: 崧幼博學，天性廉慎。

translations.literal: From youth Song was broadly learned, and by nature he was honest and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Song was broadly learned, and by nature he was honest and cautious.

sentences.zh: 兄弟三人共居一茆屋，有田五十畝。

translations.literal: Three brothers lived together in one thatched hut and had fifty mu of land.
translations.idiomatic: Three brothers lived together in one thatched hut on fifty mu of land.

sentences.zh: 及貴，無所增益。

translations.literal: When he rose to eminence, he added nothing to it.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he rose to eminence, he added nothing to it.

sentences.zh: 十年一布被，鼠傷，始易之，仍葺以衣其子。

translations.literal: One cotton quilt served him for ten years; when rats damaged it he only then replaced it, yet still mended the old one with cloth for his son.
translations.idiomatic: One cotton quilt served him for ten years; when rats damaged it he only then replaced it, yet still patched the old one with scraps of clothing for his son.

sentences.zh: 居官未嘗以家累自隨。

translations.literal: While in office he never brought his household burdens with him.
translations.idiomatic: While in office he never brought his family with him.

sentences.zh: 之任北平，攜一童往，至則遣還。

translations.literal: When he went to take up his post in Beiping, he took one boy servant and, on arrival, sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: When he went to take up his post in Beiping, he took one boy servant and, on arrival, sent him back home.

sentences.zh: 晡時史退，孤燈讀書，往往達旦。

translations.literal: When the clerks withdrew in the late afternoon, he read alone by a single lamp, often until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: When the clerks withdrew in the late afternoon, he read alone by a single lamp, often until dawn.

sentences.zh: 善為詩，豫章人宗之為《西江派》雲。

translations.literal: He was skilled at poetry, and the people of Yuzhang looked to him as the founder of the "Western River School."
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at poetry, and writers of Yuzhang looked to him as the founder of the "Western River School."

sentences.zh: 羅復仁，吉水人。

translations.literal: Luo Furen was a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Furen was a native of Jishui.

sentences.zh: 少嗜學，陳友諒辟為編修。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning; Chen Youliang recruited him as Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning; Chen Youliang recruited him as compiler.

sentences.zh: 已，知其無成，遁去。

translations.literal: After a time, seeing that Youliang's cause would not succeed, he fled and left.
translations.idiomatic: After a time, seeing that Youliang's cause would not succeed, he fled.

sentences.zh: 謁太祖於九江，留置左右。

translations.literal: He presented himself to Taizu at Jiujiang and was kept close at hand.
translations.idiomatic: He presented himself to Taizu at Jiujiang and was kept close at hand.

sentences.zh: 從戰鄱陽，賫蠟書諭降江西未下諸郡，授中書諮議。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign at Poyang, carried sealed letters in wax to summon the surrender of the Jiangxi prefectures not yet taken, and was appointed Secretarial Adviser in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign at Poyang, carried sealed letters to summon the surrender of the Jiangxi prefectures not yet taken, and was appointed secretarial adviser in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從圍武昌，太祖欲招陳理降，以復仁故友諒臣也，遣入城諭，且曰：「理若來，不失富貴。」

translations.literal: When the siege of Wuchang followed, Taizu wished to summon Chen Li to surrender; because Furen had formerly been a minister of Youliang, he sent him into the city to persuade Li, saying, "If Li comes, he will not lose wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Wuchang, Taizu wished to persuade Chen Li to surrender; because Furen had formerly been a minister of Youliang, he sent him into the city to persuade Li, saying, "If Li submits, he will not lose wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 復仁頓首曰：「如陳氏遣孤得保首領，俾臣不食言於異日，臣死不憾。」

translations.literal: Furen prostrated himself and said, "If the Chen orphan is allowed to keep his life, and your subject is not made to break his word in days to come, your subject will die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: Furen prostrated himself and said, "If the Chen orphan is allowed to keep his life, and I am not made to break my word hereafter, I will die without regret."

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「汝行，吾不汝誤也。」

translations.literal: Taizu said, "Go — I will not fail you."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "Go — I will not fail you."

sentences.zh: 復仁至城下，號慟者竟日，理縋之入。

translations.literal: When Furen reached the foot of the wall, he wailed and lamented all day; Li had him lowered inside by rope.
translations.idiomatic: When Furen reached the foot of the wall, he wailed and lamented all day; Li had him lowered inside by rope.

sentences.zh: 見理大哭，陳太祖意，且曰：「大兵所向皆摧，不降且屠，城中民何罪？」

translations.literal: Seeing Li, he wept greatly, set forth Taizu's intent, and said, "Wherever the great army advances all is shattered; if you do not surrender you will be slaughtered — what crime have the people in the city committed?"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Li, he wept greatly, conveyed Taizu's intent, and said, "Wherever the great army advances all resistance is shattered; if you do not surrender you will be slaughtered — what crime have the people in the city committed?"

sentences.zh: 理聽其言，遂率官屬出降。

translations.literal: Li listened to his words and then led his officials out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li listened to his words and then led his officials out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 孫汝敬，名簡，以字行。

translations.literal: Sun Rujing, personal name Jian, was known by his style name.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Rujing, personal name Jian, was known by his style name.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年庶吉士，就學文淵閣，誦書不稱旨，即日遣戍江南。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle he became a Junior Compiler; he studied at the Pavilion of Literary Depth, and when his recitation did not please the Emperor he was that same day sent to garrison duty in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongle he became a junior compiler and studied at the Pavilion of Literary Depth; when his recitation displeased the Emperor he was that same day sent to garrison duty in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 數日復之。

translations.literal: After several days he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: After several days he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 自此刻厲為學，累遷侍講。

translations.literal: From then on he applied himself rigorously to study and rose through posts to Lecturing Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he applied himself rigorously to study and rose through posts to lecturing attendant.

sentences.zh: 仁宗時，上言時政十五事，忤旨下獄。

translations.literal: Under Renzong he submitted fifteen criticisms of current policy, offended the imperial will, and was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Renzong he submitted fifteen criticisms of current policy, offended the throne, and was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 既與李時勉同改御史，直聲震一時。

translations.literal: He was then transferred together with Li Shimian to censor, and his forthright reputation shook the age.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred together with Li Shimian to censor, and his forthright voice shook the age.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初，上書大學士楊士奇曰：「太祖高皇帝奄有四海，太宗文皇帝再造寰區。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuande he wrote to Grand Secretary Yang Shiqi, saying, "The Taizu Gao Emperor suddenly possessed the four seas, and the Taizong Wen Emperor again created order throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xuande reign he wrote to Grand Secretary Yang Shiqi, saying, "The Taizu Gao Emperor suddenly possessed the four seas, and the Taizong Wen Emperor again created order throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 然猶翼翼兢兢，無敢豫怠。

translations.literal: Yet they were still cautious and fearful, not daring to grow lax beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they remained cautious and vigilant, never daring to slacken.

sentences.zh: 先皇帝嗣統未及期月，奄棄群臣。

translations.literal: The late Emperor succeeded to the throne for less than a full month before he suddenly abandoned his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor had succeeded to the throne for less than a full month before he suddenly abandoned his ministers.

sentences.zh: 揆厥所由，皆憸壬小夫，獻金石之方以致疾也。

translations.literal: Considering the causes, it was all due to sycophantic petty men who presented elixirs of metal and stone and thereby brought on illness.
translations.idiomatic: Considering the causes, it was all due to sycophantic petty men who presented elixirs of metal and stone and thereby brought on illness.

sentences.zh: 去冬，簡以愚戇應詔上書，言涉不敬，罪當萬死。

translations.literal: Last winter Jian, in his foolish bluntness, responded to the edict with a memorial whose words touched on disrespect; the offense deserved ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Last winter I, in my foolish bluntness, responded to the edict with a memorial whose words bordered on disrespect; the offense deserved death ten thousand times over.

sentences.zh: 先皇帝憐其孤直，寬雷霆之誅，俾居方路，撫躬循省，無可稱塞。

translations.literal: The late Emperor pitied his solitary uprightness, spared him from thunderbolt punishment, and allowed him to hold a censor's post; he examined himself in reflection but had nothing with which to repay the favor.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor pitied my solitary uprightness, spared me from thunderbolt punishment, and allowed me to hold a censor's post; I have examined myself in reflection but have nothing with which to repay the favor.

sentences.zh: 伏見今年六月，車駕幸天壽山，躬謁二陵，京師之人瞻望咨嗟，以為聖天子大孝。

translations.literal: I have observed that in the sixth month of this year the imperial carriage visited Tianshou Mountain and personally paid homage at the two tombs; the people of the capital looked on with admiration and sighs, taking it as the great filial piety of the sage Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I have observed that in the sixth month of this year the imperial carriage visited Tianshou Mountain and personally paid homage at the two tombs; the people of the capital looked on with admiration and sighs, taking it as the great filial piety of the sage Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 既而道路喧傳，禮畢即較獵講武，扈從惟也先士幹與其徒數百人。

translations.literal: Then rumors spread along the roads that as soon as the rites were finished there was hunting and military drill, with only Esen Taishi and several hundred of his followers in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Then rumors spread along the roads that as soon as the rites were finished the court turned to hunting and military drill, with only Esen Taishi and several hundred of his followers in attendance.

sentences.zh: 風馳電掣，馳逐先後。

translations.literal: Like wind racing and lightning flashing, they galloped in pursuit one before another.
translations.idiomatic: Like wind racing and lightning flashing, they galloped in pursuit, jockeying for the lead.

sentences.zh: 某聞此言，心悸膽落。

translations.literal: When I heard this, my heart trembled and my courage fell.
translations.idiomatic: When I heard this, my heart trembled and my courage failed me.

sentences.zh: 夫蒐苗獼狩，固有國之常經。

translations.literal: Spring hunt, summer hunt, autumn hunt, and winter hunt are indeed the regular institutions of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Spring hunts, summer hunts, autumn hunts, and winter hunts are indeed the regular institutions of the state.

sentences.zh: 然以謁陵出，而與降將較獵於山谷間，垂堂之戒，銜橛之虞，不可不深慮也。

translations.literal: Yet to set out to visit the tombs and then compete in hunting with surrendered generals in mountain valleys — the warning against standing beneath a collapsing eave, the fear of a horse biting the bit-pole — must be deeply considered.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to set out to visit the tombs and then compete in hunting with surrendered generals in mountain valleys — the warning against standing beneath a collapsing eave, the fear of a startled horse biting the bit — must be deeply considered.

sentences.zh: 執事四朝舊臣，二聖元輔，於此不言，則孰得而言之者？

translations.literal: Your Excellency is an old minister of four reigns and chief assistant to two sage emperors; if you do not speak on this, then who can speak?
translations.idiomatic: Your Excellency is an old minister of four reigns and chief assistant to two sage emperors; if you do not speak on this, then who can?

sentences.zh: 惟特加采納，以弘靖獻之思，光弼直之義。」

translations.literal: I only ask that you give especial heed and adopt this counsel, to extend the thoughtful devotion of Jingxian and illuminate the upright integrity of Guangbi."
translations.idiomatic: I only ask that you give especial heed and adopt this counsel, to extend the thoughtful devotion of Jingxian and illuminate the upright integrity of Guangbi."

sentences.zh: 尋擢工部右侍郎，兩使安南。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Works and twice served as envoy to Annam.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to vice minister of the right in the Ministry of Works and twice served as envoy to Annam.

sentences.zh: 時黎利言其主陳皓已死，而張筵設女樂。

translations.literal: At the time Li Li said his lord Chen Hao was already dead, yet he spread banquets and set out female musicians.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Li claimed his lord Chen Hao was already dead, yet he spread banquets and set out female musicians.

sentences.zh: 汝敬叱之，利懼謝。

translations.literal: Rujing rebuked him; Li feared this and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Rujing rebuked him; Li feared this and apologized.

sentences.zh: 還督兩浙漕運，理陜西屯田，多所建置。

translations.literal: On his return he supervised grain transport in the two Zhe provinces and managed garrison farmland in Shaanxi, establishing many reforms.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he supervised grain transport in the two Zhe provinces and managed garrison farmland in Shaanxi, establishing many reforms.

sentences.zh: 坐受饋，充為事官。

translations.literal: Convicted of accepting gifts, he was reduced to a labor-service officer.
