translations.idiomatic: Convicted of accepting gifts, he was reduced to a labor-service officer.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，遇赦，汝敬誤引詔復職，復逮系。

translations.literal: When Yingzong ascended the throne there was an amnesty; Rujing mistakenly cited the edict to reclaim his post and was again arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne there was an amnesty; Rujing mistakenly cited the edict to reclaim his post and was again arrested and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 以在陜措置勞，宥死戍邊。

translations.literal: Because of his labor in arranging affairs in Shaanxi, death was spared and he was exiled to garrison the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his labor in arranging affairs in Shaanxi, death was spared and he was exiled to garrison the frontier.

sentences.zh: 尋復職，蒞故任。

translations.literal: Before long his post was restored and he took up his former duties.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his post was restored and he returned to his former duties.

sentences.zh: 塞上有警，汝敬往督餉。

translations.literal: When there was an alarm on the frontier, Rujing went to supervise supplies.
translations.idiomatic: When there was an alarm on the frontier, Rujing went to supervise supplies.

sentences.zh: 遇敵紅城子，中流矢，墜馬得免。

translations.literal: He encountered the enemy at Hongchengzi, was struck by an arrow, fell from his horse, and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He encountered the enemy at Hongchengzi, was struck by an arrow, fell from his horse, and escaped.

sentences.zh: 以疾告歸，卒。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and requested leave to return home, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and requested leave to return home, then died.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：明始建國，首以人材為務。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: When Ming first established the state, it took talent as its first task.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: When Ming first established the state, it made talent its first priority.

sentences.zh: 征辟四方，宿儒群集闕下，隨其所長而用之。

translations.literal: It recruited from the four directions; aged scholars gathered in throngs beneath the palace gate, and each was employed according to his strengths.
translations.idiomatic: It recruited from the four directions; aged scholars gathered in throngs beneath the palace gate, and each was employed according to his strengths.

sentences.zh: 自議禮定制外，或參列法從，或預直承明，而成均胄子之任尤多稱職，彬彬乎稱得人焉。

translations.literal: Apart from deliberating on ritual and establishing institutions, some served among the legal attendants, some attended duty at Chengmeng, and especially many who held posts over the imperial students performed their duties well — refined indeed, they were called men rightly chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from deliberating on ritual and establishing institutions, some served among the legal attendants, some attended duty at Chengmeng, and especially many who held posts over the imperial students performed their duties well — refined indeed, they were called men rightly chosen.

sentences.zh: 夫諸臣當元之季世，窮經績學，株守草野，幾於沒齒無聞。

translations.literal: These ministers, in the closing age of the Yuan, exhausted themselves in the classics and accumulated learning, rooted in the wilds and fields, nearly dying old without renown.
translations.idiomatic: These ministers, in the closing age of the Yuan, exhausted themselves in the classics and accumulated learning, rooted in obscurity in the wilds, nearly dying old without renown.

sentences.zh: 及乎泰運初平，連茹利見，乃各展所蘊，以潤色鴻猷，黼黼文治。

translations.literal: When the great fortune was first settled, like linked roots they met with favor, and each then unfolded what he had stored to adorn the great design and enrich civil governance.
translations.idiomatic: When fortune turned peaceful, like linked roots they rose together and met with favor, and each then unfolded what he had stored to adorn the great design and enrich civil governance.

sentences.zh: 昔人謂天下不患無才，惟視上之網羅何如耳，顧不信哉！

translations.literal: The ancients said the realm does not worry over lacking talent — it only depends on how the ruler gathers it — is this not truly so!
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said the realm never lacks talent — it only depends on how well the ruler gathers it — and is this not truly so!
